> One external check changed the implementation shape: Anthropic’s current docs still say they do not provide embeddings, and recommend Voyage for embeddings. So the plan should not literally implement “Anthropic embeddings”; it should use Voyage embeddings with the Claude/Anthropic stack unless you want a different embeddings provider.
>
> Voyage embeddings are the vector model layer, not the database.
>
> For lore retrieval, we need to turn each comic/card/transcript chunk into a numeric vector so a query like “father in stasis” can retrieve semantically related chunks even if they do not repeat the exact words. Anthropic’s current docs say Anthropic does not offer its own embedding model and recommends Voyage AI; their current example uses models like `voyage-4` and the Python package/API with `VOYAGE_API_KEY`. The vector store then persists and searches those vectors.
>
> So the clean Phase 0 default is:
> - **Voyage `voyage-4`** for embeddings, because it is the current Anthropic-recommended path.
> - **Qdrant** as the vector store, because it is simpler to run locally than adding Postgres just for `pgvector`.
> - Add `VOYAGE_API_KEY` as a required env var for full lore retrieval; tests can use a deterministic fake embedder so CI does not need the key.
>
> For the Sonnet question: I’m separating “which model we use while planning” from “which model the built game calls at runtime.” Your instruction could mean either. My recommended interpretation is Sonnet for every Phase 0 runtime role to control cost while prompt-testing, with the model tier configurable so Phase 1 can restore Opus-for-Narrator if needed.

> Cost estimate for Voyage is effectively negligible for Phase 0.
>
> Using the current [Voyage pricing page](https://docs.voyageai.com/docs/pricing): `voyage-4` is **$0.06 per million text tokens** after the first **200M free tokens** for each account. `voyage-4-lite` is $0.02/M, and `voyage-4-large` is $0.12/M.
>
> Rough Phase 0 math:
> - 446 comic pages at ~500–1,500 text tokens/page = ~223k–669k tokens.
> - 10 actor cards + narrator card + relations + test scenes likely keeps the indexed corpus under ~1M tokens.
> - One full re-embed with `voyage-4`: **~$0.01–$0.06** after free tier; **$0** if the 200M free tier is available.
> - Per-turn query embedding is tiny: even 720 turns × 100 tokens/query = 72k tokens = **~$0.004** after free tier.
> - Qdrant local itself is free; cost is just local disk/CPU.
>
> So embeddings are not the Phase 0 budget concern. Claude calls for OCR, Narrator evals, actor calls, and Honcho reasoning dominate. My recommendation stays **Voyage `voyage-4` + local Qdrant**, with a fake embedder for tests and `VOYAGE_API_KEY` required only for real ingestion/search.

> # Phase 0 Implementation Plan
>
> ## Summary
> Build the Phase 0 CLI-only agent loop from the current docs-first repo. The implementation starts with repo/bootstrap scaffolding, proves the Honcho API contract, then wires the Go game loop, Python Honcho sidecar, Sonnet-based actor/Narrator calls, Voyage+Qdrant lore retrieval, corpus replay, and observable exit evidence.
>
> Phase 0 runtime model policy: **Sonnet for every LLM role**. Keep model names configurable so Phase 1 can switch the Narrator to Opus without code changes.

> - Bootstrap the repo with Go module, `uv` Python sidecar, `Makefile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, and `scripts/init.sh`.
> - Copy-and-own editable lore into `lore/`: Narrator peer card, canonical actor cards from Council references, Tonto/Lothar drafts, relationship matrix, Edna research, and comic transcripts.
> - Implement the Python FastAPI Honcho sidecar with the six documented endpoints, loading `SANS_NOM_HONCHO_API_KEY` and exposing OpenAPI as the schema source for generated Go client/types.
> - Implement Go packages for scene state, prompts, actors, Narrator orchestration, bridge client, pre-filter, telemetry, and CLI testbed.
> - Use `claude -p --model sonnet` as the Phase 0 LLM adapter for Narrator, actor, audit, grader, and card-curation roles.
> - Use **Voyage `voyage-4` + local Qdrant** for lore retrieval. Add deterministic fake embeddings for tests. Voyage cost is effectively negligible for Phase 0: `voyage-4` is $0.06/M tokens after the current 200M-token free tier.
> - Add local Prometheus/Grafana/OTel collector wiring so cost, latency, lore hit rate, card updates, and actor fanout are visible before Phase 1.
>
> ## Interfaces
> - Sidecar endpoints: `/v1/health`, `/v1/scene/context`, `/v1/scene/commit`, `/v1/peer/{id}/card` GET/PATCH, `/v1/repr`.
> - Required env: `SANS_NOM_HONCHO_API_KEY`, `SIDECAR_TOKEN`, `VOYAGE_API_KEY`, `QDRANT_URL`, `SANS_NOM_MODEL=sonnet`.
> - Regression scene files: `testdata/scenes/*.yaml` with `id`, initial scene state, player input, expected actors, reference output, and human grading checks.
> - CLI capabilities: fresh workspace seed, manual scene play, replay one corpus scene, run full corpus, run Tonto-of-Edna verification, show summary/pass-fail report.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Day-0 Honcho smoke test: confirm current SDK behavior for peer creation, `set_card(target=...)`, session peer config with `observe_others=True`, message commit, and directional context/query.
> - Unit tests: pre-filter, prompt assembly, actor-output parsing, scene schema parsing, sidecar auth, card update/eviction policy, fake lore retrieval.
> - Integration tests: Go bridge against mocked sidecar, Python sidecar against mocked Honcho SDK, Qdrant+fake embeddings, seed-honcho idempotency.
> - Live Phase 0 gates: 10-scene toy CLI playthrough, Tonto-of-Edna verification, 20-scene regression corpus, lore query corpus with cold miss rate below 30%, dashboard showing at least one full turn trace.
> - Pre-filter acceptance: injection and role-prefix true positives, abuse fixture blocking, and normal-input false-positive rate below 1%.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - Phase 0 has no web frontend, image generation, TTS, monetization, or generated-NPC production use.
> - Regression corpus means **20 total scenes**, with **5 adversarial scenes**, matching Phase 0 deliverables.
> - Actor cards are copied into `lore/actors/` rather than symlinked because Phase 0 requires game-specific edits.
> - External docs checked: [Honcho SDK v3](https://docs.honcho.dev/v3/documentation/reference/sdk), [Honcho peer cards](https://docs.honcho.dev/v3/documentation/features/advanced/peer-card), [Anthropic embeddings guidance](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/embeddings), and [Voyage pricing](https://docs.voyageai.com/docs/pricing).
</details>

> # Phase 0 Implementation Plan
>
> ## Summary
> Build the Phase 0 CLI-only testbed for **Sans-Nom**, not a Council of Castaka clone. Council of Castaka is reference material only: it supplies high-quality character cards, relationship-matrix examples, and proof that the lore can be encoded well. Its council mechanics, all-characters-present premise, and Sans-Nom/Opus role assignment do **not** transfer into this game.
>
> The core implementation centers on a **creative-writer Narrator** whose peer card absorbs Metabarons traits, laws, tone, and character constraints. The Narrator authors the story; character lore is used as grounding and pressure, not as a resurrection mechanism where every canonical figure exists in the same room.
>
> Phase 0 runtime model policy: **Sonnet for every LLM role in this phase**, via `claude -p`, with model names configurable for later phases.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Bootstrap the repo with Go module, Python `uv` sidecar, `Makefile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, and `scripts/init.sh`.
> - Create owned game lore under `lore/`: Narrator peer card, adapted actor/reference cards, relationship matrix, Tonto/Lothar material, Edna research, and comic transcripts.
> - Treat Council cards as source references for encoding quality. Copy/adapt only what serves the game’s childhood/dynasty story; do not inherit council summoning, debate, all-cast invocation, or Opus Sans-Nom defaults.
> - Implement the Python FastAPI Honcho sidecar with the documented Phase 0 endpoints and generated Go client/types from OpenAPI.
> - Implement Go packages for scene state, prompt assembly, Narrator orchestration, selective character grounding, bridge client, pre-filter, telemetry, and Bubble Tea CLI.
> - Use **Voyage `voyage-4` + local Qdrant** for lore retrieval, with fake deterministic embeddings for tests.
>
> ## Core Behavior
> - The Narrator owns story creation. It receives the player input, scene state, Sans-Nom state, relevant Honcho context, and retrieved canon snippets.
> - Character cards constrain the Narrator’s authorship and may be used for scoped actor-style checks only when a character is actually present, remembered, narrated by Tonto, or otherwise valid in the scene.
> - The implementation must prevent accidental “council mode”: no default all-character fanout, no resurrected ancestor roster, no simultaneous dynasty roundtable unless the game scene explicitly earns it.
> - Honcho stores witness-bound memory: one peer per relevant entity, sessions per location arc, directional cards/representations only for characters who actually witness or legitimately remember events.
>
> ## Interfaces
> - Sidecar endpoints: `/v1/health`, `/v1/scene/context`, `/v1/scene/commit`, `/v1/peer/{id}/card` GET/PATCH, `/v1/repr`.
> - Required env: `SANS_NOM_HONCHO_API_KEY`, `SIDECAR_TOKEN`, `VOYAGE_API_KEY`, `QDRANT_URL`, `SANS_NOM_MODEL=sonnet`.
> - CLI capabilities: seed workspace, play manual scene, replay one corpus scene, run full corpus, run Tonto-of-Edna verification, show pass/fail summary.
> - Regression scene format: scene state, player input, expected grounding sources, reference Narrator output, and human grading checks.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Honcho spike first: verify peer creation, directional `set_card(target=...)`, `observe_others=True`, message commit, and directional context/query against the real SDK.
> - Unit tests: pre-filter, prompt assembly, scene schema parsing, bridge auth, fake retrieval, card loading, and “no accidental all-cast invocation” guard.
> - Integration tests: Go bridge against mocked sidecar, Python sidecar against mocked Honcho, Qdrant with fake embeddings, seed-honcho idempotency.
> - Phase 0 gates: 10-scene toy playthrough, Tonto-of-Edna verification, 20-scene regression corpus, lore query corpus with cold miss rate below 30%, and dashboard trace for at least one full turn.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - No web frontend, image generation, TTS, monetization, or generated-NPC production use in Phase 0.
> - Council of Castaka is a lore/prompt-quality reference, not a mechanics source.
> - Sonnet is used for all Phase 0 runtime LLM calls, despite Council’s Sans-Nom using Opus.
> - Voyage embeddings are effectively not a Phase 0 cost driver; Claude calls, OCR, Honcho reasoning, and playtest loops dominate cost.

> I need a blunt answer, do we need to refine the specs first ?

Yes.

Not because the whole design is unclear, but because a few specs are still loose enough that implementation would bake in the wrong assumptions:

1. **Council reference boundary**
   Must explicitly say Council is a lore/card-quality reference, not a mechanics template. Otherwise someone will overbuild actor fanout or all-cast invocation.

2. **Narrator vs actor role**
   The game is driven by the creative-writer Narrator. Actor cards are grounding material and selective scene inputs, not equal co-authors on every turn. This needs to be written cleanly.

3. **Model policy**
   “Sonnet for all roles in Phase 0” should be stated as a Phase 0 implementation constraint, with later phases configurable.

4. **Lore retrieval choice**
   Lock **Voyage + Qdrant** now. That decision affects sidecar deps, Docker, ingestion, and tests.

5. **Phase 0 acceptance artifacts**
   Define exactly what proves success: toy scenario, regression corpus format, Tonto-of-Edna output, and telemetry screenshot/query.

So: **yes, refine the specs first, but narrowly.** I would do a short spec pass before code, not another big design cycle. The target is probably 4–6 docs touched, then implementation can start cleanly.

Better: writer outputs a structured “story packet” with beats, choices, gates, actor needs, and memory intents; the Narrator turns only the currently selected path into player-facing prose and commits only canonical rolled-out events to Honcho.
>
> I need to resolve one contradiction before locking the spec: you selected “full authored tree,” but then described the structured packet approach. Those can coexist if “full authored” means the full decision structure, not prewritten final prose.
>
> Plan
>
> # Phase 0 Revised Plan: Writer/Narrator Split
>
> ## Summary
> Implement Phase 0 around two authoring layers:
>
> - **Creative Writer**: slower background planner. It creates a structured full decision tree for the current story chunk.
> - **Narrator**: fast foreground layer. It rolls out the selected node, calls relevant actors, rewrites the chosen path into player-facing prose, presents choices, and commits witnessed canon to Honcho.
>
> “Full tree” means full structure for the current bounded chunk, not the whole game. Phase 0 target: one active packet of roughly 3–5 scene nodes, revised after each user decision.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a `StoryPacket` schema with: packet id, context snapshot, scene nodes, beats, gates, choices, actor needs, memory intents, and invalidation/revision notes.
> - Creative Writer runs asynchronously using Sonnet via `claude -p`. It receives the latest committed Narrator prose, user decision, current scene state, and updated Honcho representations.
> - Narrator receives only the active packet node plus current context. It writes final prose for the chosen path and does not expose Writer drafts.
> - Actor calls are managed by the Narrator, only for characters actually present, remembered, narrated, or valid for the current scene.
> - Honcho memory writes are **directional/witness-bound**: commit only what each peer actually witnessed. No global dump of all actor interiors.
> - Council of Castaka remains a lore/card-quality reference only. No council mechanics, no all-cast fanout, no resurrected dynasty roster.
>
> ## Memory Policy
> - Commit player decisions, final Narrator prose, surfaced actor speech/actions, scene metadata, and witness lists.
> - Actor private interior can inform the Narrator, but must not leak into another peer’s witnessed memory.
> - If Phase 0 needs actor self-evolution from hidden reactions, store that in a private actor-scoped/non-shared channel, not the shared scene session.
> - Writer drafts and unused branches stay outside Honcho. They are planning artifacts, not canon.
>
> ## Implementation Surface
> - Go packages: `writer`, `narrator`, `scene`, `actors`, `prompt`, `bridge`, `lore`, `prefilter`, `telemetry`, `cli`.
> - Python sidecar: Honcho endpoints from the existing spec plus schema-generated Go client/types.
> - Lore retrieval: **Voyage `voyage-4` + local Qdrant**, with deterministic fake embeddings for tests.
> - Runtime model policy: Sonnet for all Phase 0 roles, configurable for later phases.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit-test `StoryPacket` parsing, node selection, gate handling, packet revision, and “no unused branch committed to Honcho.”
> - Integration-test Narrator rollout from a packet node through actor calls and directional Honcho commit.
> - Add a specific regression guard for “no accidental council mode”: no all-character default fanout.
> - Phase 0 gates remain: 10-scene toy playthrough, Tonto-of-Edna verification, 20-scene corpus, lore retrieval cold miss rate below 30%, and visible telemetry trace.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - Phase 0 proves the Writer/Narrator split in CLI only.
> - The Writer plans structure; the Narrator owns final prose.
> - Honcho is the authority for evolved representations, not for unrolled future plans.
> - External grounding checked: [Honcho SDK](https://docs.honcho.dev/v3/documentation/reference/sdk), [Honcho peer cards](https://docs.honcho.dev/v3/documentation/features/advanced/peer-card), [Anthropic embeddings note](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/embeddings), [Voyage pricing](https://docs.voyageai.com/docs/pricing).
</details>

Aiming for a structured full tree is realistic if Phase 0 bounds it to one chunk, not a whole playthrough. The critical safety issue is memory: raw actor interiors cannot go into the same witnessed Honcho session as player-visible canon, or Sans-Nom/other peers may learn thoughts they did not witness.

> well time to test, first we need to ingest the lore, whats your plan for that ?

My plan: **do ingestion in two passes, text first, comics second.**

1. **Text corpus first**
   Ingest what we already have:
   - `lore/narrator/peer-card.md`
   - `lore/actors/*.md`
   - `external/references/council of castaka/metabarons/*.md`
   - `external/references/.../relations/*`
   - docs that encode game rules, especially `docs/mechanics/world/ip-commitments.md`

   This gives us a working retrieval loop before touching 446 comic pages.

2. **Build ingestion script**
   Add a Python module/script using the sidecar deps:
   - read markdown files
   - chunk by heading/paragraph with source metadata
   - embed chunks with `SANS_NOM_VOYAGE_API_KEY` using `voyage-4`
   - upsert into local Qdrant collection, probably `sans_nom_lore`
   - write a local manifest with source hash so re-ingest only updates changed files

3. **Add query smoke tests**
   Before comics, validate queries like:
   - `Aghora grief Steelhead stasis pod`
   - `Tonto tells old stories`
   - `Bushitaka law`
   - `Honorata tenderness control`
   - `Sans-Nom name weight`

   Pass bar: relevant chunks appear in top 5.

4. **Comic OCR second**
   Process `external/comics/meta-barons/*.jpg` into reviewed transcripts under:
   - `lore/canon/comics/page-001.md`
   - etc.

   I would not dump OCR straight into Qdrant as canon without review. First pass can be marked `review_status: raw_ocr`; reviewed pages become `review_status: reviewed`.

5. **Ingest reviewed transcripts**
   Once transcripts exist, same script indexes them with page metadata:
   - page number
   - source image filename
   - review status
   - chunk id
   - character tags if known

6. **Wire runtime search**
   Then the Narrator/Writer context can call lore search and receive top-k snippets. Until Qdrant is populated, keep fake retrieval for tests.

Bluntly: **start with text-card ingestion today. Do not begin with comic OCR.** We need to prove retrieval plumbing before spending tokens and time on 446 images.

> Plan

> # Lore Extraction Plan From Comic Pages
>
> ## Summary
> Create a resumable vision pipeline that turns the 446 page images into usable lore data, then indexes that data into Qdrant. The pipeline uses one isolated Sonnet vision worker per page, then reconciles pages into comic-level summaries and extracts structured character data.
>
> This will produce enough text/JSON lore to let you move the image files out of the repo while keeping source filenames and hashes for traceability.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a comic ingestion script that builds a manifest from `external/comics/meta-barons/*.jpg`, parsing volume number, page label, spread/single-page status, file path, and SHA-256.
> - Add page-worker extraction using `claude -p --model sonnet` with a strict JSON schema. Each worker reads one image and writes one page summary file.
> - Store page outputs under `lore/canon/comics/pages/`, one JSON per source image.
> - Add a reconciler pass that groups page JSON by comic volume and writes volume lore summaries under `lore/canon/comics/volumes/`.
> - Add a character extraction pass that reads all page/volume summaries and writes per-character structured data under `lore/canon/comics/characters/`.
> - Add Qdrant ingestion for page summaries, volume summaries, and character facts using `SANS_NOM_VOYAGE_API_KEY` with `voyage-4`.
>
> ## Extraction Shape
> - Page summaries are **not full transcripts**. They capture plot events, visual facts, character presence, locations, dialogue meaning, lore facts, uncertainties, and source refs.
> - Volume summaries reconcile continuity across pages: chronology, major events, recurring motifs, lore laws, character arcs, and open uncertainties.
> - Character files capture aliases, appearances, traits, relationships, witnessed facts, knowledge boundaries, important actions, voice notes, and source page refs.
> - Every extracted fact keeps `source_image`, `page_id`, and `image_sha256` so the summaries remain auditable after images move out.
>
> ## Execution Strategy
> - Use bounded parallelism, not 446 simultaneous processes. Default: 4 concurrent page workers.
> - Each page worker is independent and resumable: if output exists and the image hash matches, skip it.
> - Use atomic writes: write `.tmp`, validate JSON, then rename.
> - Retry low-confidence pages once with higher effort. Remaining failures go into `lore/canon/comics/review-needed.jsonl`.
> - Run order:
>   1. Dry run on 3 pages: one normal page, one spread, one dialogue-heavy page.
>   2. Process volume 1 end to end.
>   3. Reconcile volume 1 and extract character facts.
>   4. If quality is good, process all 446 pages.
>   5. Ingest generated lore text into Qdrant.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Schema validation for page, volume, and character JSON.
> - Resume test: rerunning does not regenerate unchanged pages.
> - No-canon-pollution test: image summaries are indexed as lore references, not Honcho scene memory.
> - Retrieval smoke tests after Qdrant ingest:
>   - `Tonto tells a story`
>   - `Metabunker city-shaft`
>   - `Aghora grief Steelhead`
>   - `Honorata control tenderness`
>   - `Bushitaka law`
> - Acceptance: top 5 retrieval results include relevant page/volume/character sources for the smoke queries.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - Use Sonnet for all extraction/reconciliation roles.
> - Do not preserve full verbatim comic text; preserve summarized lore and short source-grounded notes.
> - The page images stay in place until the manifest, summaries, reconciled volumes, character files, and Qdrant ingest pass are complete.
</details>

> Plan
>
> # Agentic Honcho Peer-Card Generation Plan
>
> ## Summary
> Generate **116 Honcho-ready peer cards**, one per unique `character_id`, by aggregating the existing 212 extracted character records. Each card is produced by a creative Writer loop and accepted only after a strict Verifier approves content, grounding, and Honcho format.
>
> Writer: `claude -p --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --effort max`  
> Verifier: `codex exec --ephemeral -m gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="xhigh"`  
> Default loop: unbounded until accepted, resumable, interrupt-safe.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a `peer-cards` Python CLI alongside `comic-lore` with commands:
>   - `generate`: aggregate records and run Writer/Verifier loops.
>   - `status`: show accepted/pending/blocked card counts.
>   - `validate`: strict local validation of staged cards.
>   - `seed-honcho --workspace-id ...`: optional staging Honcho seed, never automatic.
> - Save artifacts under `lore/canon/comics/peer-cards/staging/`:
>   - One JSON artifact per peer with `character_id`, aliases, source files, source refs, final `card: list[str]`, verifier report, model metadata, and iteration count.
>   - Per-iteration drafts/reports kept for audit and resume.
> - Peer card format:
>   - `card` is the exact Honcho payload: `list[str]`, max 40 facts.
>   - Allowed prefixes: `Name:`, `ALIAS:`, `ROLE:`, `TRAIT:`, `RELATIONSHIP:`, `VOICE:`, `INSTRUCTION:`, `BOUNDARY:`.
>   - Source refs stay in artifact metadata, not in Honcho card facts.
>   - Facts must be durable, atomic, non-transient, and useful to actor/writer/narrator behavior.
> - Source aggregation:
>   - Merge all `characters-volume-*.json` records by `character_id`.
>   - Include relevant page refs, volume summaries, relationships, actions, witnessed facts, voice notes, and existing traits.
>   - For known Council reference cards, use them only as card-quality/canon-style support, not as council mechanics.
> - Writer behavior:
>   - Produces passion-encoded cards: contradictions, obsessions, taboos, voice, durable traits, and canon boundaries.
>   - May infer traits from source-grounded actions, but must not invent unsupported biography.
>   - Must not introduce council mode, all-cast fanout, resurrection roster assumptions, or non-witnessed knowledge.
> - Verifier behavior:
>   - Returns strict JSON: `accepted`, `blocking_issues`, `unsupported_claims`, `format_errors`, `missing_opportunities`, `revision_instructions`.
>   - Rejects empty/weak traiting for meaningful characters, unsupported claims, generic sci-fi flattening, markdown, duplicate facts, over-40 cards, and non-Honcho-shaped content.
>   - Can mark a card `blocked_source_insufficient` only when the source bundle cannot support a useful peer card; blocked cards are not seeded.
>
> ## Honcho Staging
> - Local staging files are the source of truth.
> - Honcho seeding is opt-in only:
>   - `peer-cards seed-honcho --workspace-id sans-nom-peer-card-staging --replace`
> - Seeding uses existing sidecar/Honcho semantics: `set_card`/replace for each peer’s own card.
> - Directional cards are out of scope for this pass; this pass creates base peer cards only.
> - Honcho constraints follow current docs: peer cards are `list[str]`, max 40 facts, and `set_card()` replaces the whole card. Source: [Honcho Peer Card docs](https://docs.honcho.dev/v3/documentation/features/advanced/peer-card).
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit tests:
>   - Aggregation reduces 212 records to 116 unique peer bundles.
>   - Card schema rejects missing card, over-40 facts, bad prefixes, markdown, duplicate facts, and empty accepted cards.
>   - Fake Writer/Verifier loop revises until accepted and resumes without rerunning accepted cards.
>   - `seed-honcho` dry run and in-memory HonchoOps replace behavior work without touching live Honcho.
> - Regression tests:
>   - No accidental council mode phrases or all-cast fanout instructions.
>   - No source refs embedded in the Honcho `card` list.
>   - No seeding happens during `generate`.
> - Acceptance checks:
>   - `peer-cards generate` eventually produces 116 accepted staging artifacts or explicit blocked reports.
>   - `peer-cards validate` passes.
>   - Smoke cards for Tonto, Othon, Honorata, Aghora, Steelhead, Bushitaka show strong traits and usable voice/instruction facts.
>   - Optional Honcho seed writes and reads back the same card lists from the staging workspace.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - Scope is **116 unique peer cards**, not 212 per-volume samples.
> - Volume `character_arcs` stay unchanged for now; peer cards become the richer character-arc artifact.
> - Writer model failure is a hard failure: do not silently fall back from `claude-sonnet-4-6`.
> - Verifier model failure is a hard failure: do not silently fall back from `gpt-5.5 xhigh`.
> - Default generation is expensive and long-running; it uses bounded parallelism, resumable state, atomic writes, and no hard iteration cap unless `--max-iterations` is explicitly passed for debugging.
</details>

One important implementation detail surfaced: the current extraction has 212 character records but only 116 unique `character_id`s. Honcho cards are keyed by peer, so duplicate IDs cannot all be seeded as the same card without either aggregation or record-specific staging IDs.

Yes. Do a **peer identity resolution pass before peer-card writing**.

The right intermediate artifact is something like:

```json
{
  "peer_card_id": "steelhead__late-sealed",
  "display_name": "Steelhead",
  "merge_policy": "kept_separate",
  "reason": "Late Steelhead has incompatible traits/voice/state from warrior-era Steelhead.",
  "source_records": [
    {
      "character_id": "steelhead",
      "file": "lore/canon/comics/characters/characters-volume-16.json",
      "volumes": [16],
      "page_ids": ["..."]
    }
  ]
}
```

So the pipeline becomes:

1. **Identity map pass**
   - Input: all `characters-volume-*.json` plus volume summaries.
   - Sonnet decides whether duplicate `character_id`s represent one stable peer or multiple phase-specific peers.
   - Output: `lore/canon/comics/peer-cards/identity-map.json`.

2. **Peer-card pass**
   - One card per `peer_card_id`, not per raw `character_id`.
   - Each card receives only the source records assigned to that peer identity.
   - This preserves kid/adult, pre/post trauma, transformed, sealed, dead/remembered, narrator-only, and role-shifted variants.

3. **Verifier pass**
   - Verifies the split/merge decision and later verifies each card.
   - Rejects cards that mix incompatible arcs into one Honcho peer.

Key point: Honcho peer IDs should represent **a coherent actor/writer persona**, not merely a canonical name. Same name can become multiple peer IDs when the traits would fight each other in generation.

I’d implement this as a new first command:

```bash
uv run --project bridge peer-cards identity-map
```

Then generation consumes that map:

```bash
uv run --project bridge peer-cards generate
```

Default output should be `peer_card_id => source character records`, with explicit merge/split reasons.

> # Peer-Card Writer/Verifier Loop Plan
>
> ## Summary
> Build the next `peer-cards` phase: generate Honcho-ready cards for the 124 resolved `peer_card_id`s in `identity-map.json`. Each card runs through a file-based agent loop: **Sonnet 4.6 max** writes the card, **Codex GPT-5.5 xhigh** verifies it, and verifier feedback is fed back into Sonnet until accepted.
>
> The models never receive large lore payloads inline. Each iteration writes a compact input bundle to disk; prompts contain clean instructions plus file paths.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Extend the `peer-cards` CLI:
>   - `generate`: run writer/verifier loops for pending peers.
>   - `status`: include accepted/pending/blocked/in-progress counts.
>   - `validate`: validate identity map plus staged card artifacts.
>   - `seed-honcho --workspace-id ... --replace`: optional only, never part of generation.
> - Store artifacts under `lore/canon/comics/peer-cards/staging/{peer_card_id}/`:
>   - `input.json`: identity, source records, volume context, optional Council/cast refs.
>   - `iterations/NN-draft.json`: Sonnet card candidate.
>   - `iterations/NN-review.json`: Codex verifier report.
>   - `card.json`: accepted final artifact with `card: list[str]`, metadata, source refs, and verifier approval.
>   - `blocked.json`: only if verifier marks source insufficient.
> - Sonnet writer command:
>   - `claude --model claude-sonnet-4-6 -p --effort max --no-session-persistence --permission-mode bypassPermissions --add-dir <repo-root> --output-format json --json-schema <inline schema>`
>   - Prompt gives role/task only, points to `input.json`, and includes prior verifier feedback file path on revisions.
> - Codex verifier command:
>   - `codex exec --ephemeral --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -C <repo-root> -m gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="xhigh" --output-schema <schema> -o <tmp-review.json>`
>   - Verifier reads `input.json` and draft file, returns strict review JSON only.
> - Loop behavior:
>   - Default `--max-iterations 0` means no hard cap.
>   - Resume skips accepted cards and resumes from the next iteration for unfinished peers.
>   - `--workers` defaults to `1` for cost/control; higher values allowed.
>   - Model failure is hard failure; no fallback model.
>
> ## Card Contract
> - Final Honcho payload is exactly `card: list[str]`, max 40 facts.
> - Allowed prefixes: `Name:`, `ALIAS:`, `ROLE:`, `TRAIT:`, `RELATIONSHIP:`, `VOICE:`, `INSTRUCTION:`, `BOUNDARY:`.
> - Source refs stay in artifact metadata, not inside card facts.
> - Writer must produce passion-encoded actor/writer/narrator utility: contradictions, desires, taboos, voice, boundaries, relationship posture.
> - Verifier rejects unsupported canon, weak/generic traits, markdown, duplicate facts, over-40 cards, source refs inside cards, council-mode language, and phase-mixing against `identity-map.json`.
>

> - Unit tests:

>   - Validate card prefix rules, 40-fact cap, no markdown, no source refs in facts.

>   - Resume skips accepted cards and does not overwrite without `--force`.
>   - `seed-honcho` dry-run/in-memory mode replaces cards correctly.
> - Regression tests:
>   - No accidental council mode or all-cast fanout phrases.
>   - Steelhead split peers do not share one flattened card.
>   - Generate never seeds Honcho.
> - Acceptance:
>   - `peer-cards generate --peer-id tonto` writes an accepted card.
>   - Smoke set passes for `tonto`, `othon-von-salza`, `honorata__living`, `honorata__in-oda`, `steelhead__warrior`, `steelhead__late`, `aghora`, `aghnar__late`, `bushitaka`.
>   - Full run eventually yields either accepted `card.json` or explicit `blocked.json` for all 124 peer identities.

>

> Plan
>
> # Peer-Card Writer/Verifier Loop Plan
>
> ## Summary
> Generate Honcho-ready peer cards for the 124 resolved `peer_card_id`s in `identity-map.json`. Each card uses a file-based loop: **Sonnet 4.6 max** writes, **Codex GPT-5.5 xhigh** verifies, and verifier feedback loops back until accepted or explicitly blocked.
>
> For split/phase personas, every prompt must emphasize that the card is for one coherent phase, not the whole named character.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Extend `peer-cards` with:
>   - `generate`: run writer/verifier loops.
>   - `status`: show accepted/pending/blocked/in-progress.
>   - `validate`: validate identity map and staged cards.
>   - `seed-honcho --workspace-id ... --replace`: optional only.
> - Create a shared context map at `lore/canon/comics/peer-cards/context-entrypoints.json`:
>   - `identity_map`: full peer identity map.
>   - `characters`: extracted character files.
>   - `volumes`: reconciled volume summaries.
>   - `pages`: page summaries for source refs.
>   - `council_refs`: Council cards, used as card-quality/canon references only.
>   - `cast_docs`: game-side cast overlays.
>   - `narrator_card`, `glossary`, `card_seeding_docs`: project constraints and Honcho card rules.
> - Per-peer staging lives under `peer-cards/staging/{peer_card_id}/`:
>   - `input.json`: selected peer identity, source records, related identities, relationship candidates, source refs, and context-entrypoint paths.
>   - `iterations/NN-draft.json`: Sonnet draft.
>   - `iterations/NN-review.json`: Codex verifier report.
>   - `card.json`: accepted final artifact.
>   - `blocked.json`: source-insufficient only.
>
> ## Writer/Verifier Contract
> - Sonnet command: `claude --model claude-sonnet-4-6 -p --effort max --no-session-persistence --permission-mode bypassPermissions --add-dir <repo-root> --output-format json --json-schema <schema>`.
> - Codex verifier command: `codex exec --ephemeral --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -C <repo-root> -m gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="xhigh" --output-schema <schema> -o <tmp-review.json>`.
> - Prompts contain instructions and file paths only; large lore payloads are never inline.
> - Every writer input includes:
>   - full `identity-map.json` path,
>   - current `peer_card_id`,
>   - same-root split personas,
>   - related peer IDs derived from aliases/relationship text,
>   - context-entrypoint path map with descriptions.
> - For split personas, the writer must include a phase-boundary note in the artifact and avoid whole-life flattening.
> - Relationship facts must resolve to peer identities when possible:
>   - `RELATIONSHIP: steelhead__late (Steelhead): ...`
>   - If unresolved, verifier flags it unless the source genuinely lacks enough identity information.
>
> ## Card Contract
> - Final Honcho payload is `card: list[str]`, max 40 facts.
> - Allowed prefixes: `Name:`, `ALIAS:`, `ROLE:`, `TRAIT:`, `RELATIONSHIP:`, `VOICE:`, `INSTRUCTION:`, `BOUNDARY:`.
> - Source refs stay in metadata, not card facts.
> - Verifier rejects unsupported canon, generic traits, markdown, source refs inside facts, phase-mixing, raw ambiguous relationship names, council-mode language, and all-cast fanout assumptions.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit tests:
>   - Build context-entrypoint map.
>   - Build peer input with full identity-map path and related split personas.
>   - Validate relationship facts reference known `peer_card_id`s where possible.
>   - Fake writer/verifier loop revises then accepts.
>   - Resume skips accepted cards.
> - Regression tests:
>   - Steelhead split cards stay phase-specific.
>   - Honorata living/reborn/in-Oda do not collapse.
>   - Generate never seeds Honcho.
> - Acceptance:
>   - Smoke cards pass for Tonto, Othon, Honorata phases, Steelhead phases, Aghora, Aghnar late, and Bushitaka.
>   - Full run yields `card.json` or `blocked.json` for all 124 identities.
>   - `make test` and `peer-cards validate --strict` pass.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - Current `identity-map.json` is authoritative.
> - Directional cards remain out of scope.
> - Honcho seeding remains opt-in after local validation.
</details>

The key thing is your local orchestration is now the leverage point: keep jobs resumable, artifact-backed, and aggressively bounded, then you can run big speculative passes without trusting any single model call to behave. Codex becomes the worker pool, not the source of truth.

> I have no idea , but what we're doing in that loop is tight

Yeah. The loop has the right shape now:

source artifact -> writer draft -> strict verifier -> atomic staged card -> retry/resume

And the important part is that failures are contained. A bad stream, a stuck verifier, or a weak draft doesn’t poison the corpus or block the whole pass. It either retries, gets revised, or becomes an explicit review item. That’s why it can scale.

> # Phase 1 Plan: Lore Index
>
> ## Summary
> Build a dedicated `lore-index` CLI that turns the committed canon artifacts into a stable searchable corpus, then embeds it into Qdrant with Voyage. This phase protects the extracted lore before image files move out and gives the Writer/Narrator loop a real retrieval substrate.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add `lore-index` as a Python CLI in the bridge package, reusing existing `comic_lore` schemas/loaders and `lore_ops` env helpers.
> - Write tracked index artifacts under `lore/canon/index/`:
>   - `documents.jsonl`: one indexed document per page, volume, character record, accepted peer card, non-peer lore artifact, wiki section, link-matrix section, and identity-map entry.
>   - `manifest.json`: counts by kind, source paths, source SHA-256 hashes, text hashes, generated timestamp, embedding model, and collection name.
> - Add commands:
>   - `lore-index build --root .`
>   - `lore-index validate --root . --strict`
>   - `lore-index status --root .`
>   - `lore-index ingest --root . --collection sans_nom_lore --replace`
>   - `lore-index smoke --root . --collection sans_nom_lore --strict`
> - Use deterministic `doc_id` values and UUIDv5 Qdrant point IDs so rebuilds are stable.
> - Keep `comic-lore ingest-qdrant` as a compatibility wrapper or deprecate it internally to call the new index builder, avoiding two document pipelines.
> - Update `Makefile` with `lore-index-build`, `lore-index-validate`, `lore-index-ingest`, and `lore-index-smoke`.
>
> ## Index Shape
> - `comic_page:<page_id>` includes visual summary, plot events, dialogue meaning, lore facts, character facts, locations, uncertainty notes, volume/page metadata, image hash, and source image path.
> - `comic_volume:volume-XX` includes chronology, major events, motifs, lore laws, character arcs if present, locations, and uncertainties.
> - `character_record:<file>#<index>:<character_id>` preserves per-volume character arcs instead of flattening them into a single identity.
> - `peer_card:<peer_id>` indexes accepted Honcho card facts as high-signal behavioral lore.
> - `non_peer_lore:<id>` indexes verifier-approved non-peer decisions as lore references, not actor candidates.
> - `wiki_lore:<heading>` and `link_matrix:<heading>` chunk markdown by heading, with paragraph fallback if a section exceeds 6000 chars.
> - Payloads include `kind`, `source_path`, `source_sha256`, `text_sha256`, `volume`, `page_id`, `character_id`, `peer_id`, and `heading` where applicable.
>
> ## Retrieval And Smoke Tests
> - Embed documents with `SANS_NOM_VOYAGE_API_KEY`, `SANS_NOM_VOYAGE_MODEL` defaulting to `voyage-4`, and `input_type="document"`.
> - Embed queries with `input_type="query"`.
> - Qdrant default collection remains `sans_nom_lore`; `--replace` is required to recreate the collection.
> - Strict smoke queries must pass with relevant top-5 hits:
>   - `Tonto tells a story`
>   - `Metabunker city-shaft`
>   - `Aghora grief Steelhead`
>   - `Honorata control tenderness`
>   - `Bushitaka law`
>   - `Lothar is Steelhead`
>   - `Sans Nom ends the dynasty`
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit-test document building from tmp fixtures for pages, volumes, character records, peer cards, non-peer lore, wiki markdown, and link matrix markdown.
> - Unit-test stable `doc_id`, UUIDv5 point IDs, duplicate rejection, hash changes, and strict validation failures.
> - Unit-test dry-run/fake ingestion without network access using deterministic fake embeddings.
> - Regression-test that per-volume character records are indexed separately and not swallowed by peer-card aggregation.
> - Run:
>   - `uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q`
>   - `go test ./...`
>   - `uv run --project bridge lore-index --root . build`
>   - `uv run --project bridge lore-index --root . validate --strict`
>   - with Qdrant running: `uv run --project bridge lore-index --root . ingest --replace`
>   - then: `uv run --project bridge lore-index --root . smoke --strict`
>
> ## Assumptions
> - The index artifacts in `lore/canon/index/` should be committed because they are the auditable text replacement for the image corpus.
> - Qdrant storage itself is not committed.
> - Phase 1 does not add incremental file watching; rebuild-and-replace is enough for the first durable retrieval pass.
> - The Writer/Narrator loop starts only after strict smoke retrieval passes.
</details>

> # Phase 1b Plan: Runtime Lore Retrieval
>
> ## Summary
> Expose the committed Qdrant lore index through the Python bridge and add a Go retriever that the runtime can call. This makes lore retrieval usable by the CLI/game loop while keeping fake in-memory retrieval for unit tests.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add `POST /v1/lore/search` to the bridge.
>   - Request: `query`, `k`, optional filters `kind`, `peer_id`, `character_id`, `volume`.
>   - Response snippets: `doc_id`, `text`, `source_path`, `score`, `kind`, optional `page_id`, `peer_id`, `character_id`, `volume`, and raw payload.
>   - Use Voyage `input_type="query"` and Qdrant collection `sans_nom_lore` by default.
> - Extend bridge models and tests.
>   - Replace the current minimal lore models with the richer request/response shape.
>   - Add FastAPI tests that mock the lore backend and verify auth, filters, score ordering, and empty results.
> - Add Go runtime client support.
>   - Extend `internal/bridge.Client` with `LoreSearch(ctx, req)`.
>   - Add `internal/lore.BridgeRetriever` implementing the existing `Retriever` interface.
>   - Keep `MemoryIndex` and `FakeEmbedder` unchanged for pure unit tests.
> - Add retrieval telemetry.
>   - Emit `lore.search` with query SHA-256, latency ms, requested `k`, hit count, top score, miss flag, and filters.
>   - Do not log raw query text by default.
> - Add CLI smoke surface.
>   - Add a lightweight mode to `cmd/cli`: `-lore-search "Lothar is Steelhead"` with optional `-k`.
>   - It calls the bridge endpoint and prints ranked `score doc_id source_path` lines plus a short text preview.
>
> ## Implementation Notes
> - Bridge search should fail clearly when `SANS_NOM_VOYAGE_API_KEY` is missing or Qdrant is unreachable.
> - Qdrant filter fields use payload keys already written by `lore-index`: `kind`, `peer_id`, `character_id`, and `volume`.
> - Snippet text should come from the indexed payload `text`; cap returned text to a conservative preview length in the bridge response, not in Qdrant storage.
> - Default `k` is `5`; clamp to `1..20`.
> - Runtime code should not rebuild or ingest the index; it only queries an existing Qdrant collection.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Python:
>   - Unit-test filter construction and `k` clamping.
>   - FastAPI-test `/v1/lore/search` success, empty result, auth rejection, and backend error.
>   - Keep `lore-index validate --strict` as the corpus integrity gate.
> - Go:
>   - Test `Client.LoreSearch` posts the expected JSON and decodes snippets.
>   - Test `BridgeRetriever.Search` maps bridge snippets into `lore.Snippet`.
>   - Test telemetry event fields with a fake sink.
> - Integration smoke:
>   - Start sidecar and Qdrant.
>   - Run `uv run --project bridge lore-index --root . smoke --strict`.
>   - Run `go run ./cmd/cli -lore-search "Lothar is Steelhead"` and verify a relevant top-5 result.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - Phase 1b does not change Writer/Narrator prompts yet.
> - `sans_nom_lore` is already ingested before runtime search.
> - Telemetry stays local/log-oriented for now; no metrics backend is added in this phase.
</details>

Telemetry is deliberately thin but already has a sink/event shape, so the retrieval client can emit a small `lore.search` event without inventing a new observability system. I have enough to produce the implementation plan.

> Plan
>
> # Phase 1c Plan: Writer/Narrator Context Assembly
>
> ## Summary
> Add a Go context assembly layer that builds bounded, role-specific model context from the active `StoryPacket`, runtime lore retrieval, Honcho scene context, peer cards, actor needs, and witness rules. The immediate deliverable is a `-context-preview` CLI path that shows exactly what the Writer and Narrator would receive, and the normal CLI rollout will use the same Narrator context text.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a new Go package `internal/contextbundle`.
>   - `Assembler` owns context construction.
>   - Dependencies: `lore.Retriever`, bridge client interface, actor/card provider, and budget options.
>   - Outputs: `WriterContext`, `NarratorContext`, `ActorContext`, `LoreHit`, `Representation`, and `ContextBundleSummary`.
> - Extend Go bridge client with missing runtime helpers.
>   - `Representation(ctx, req)` for `/v1/repr`.
>   - `GetCard(ctx, workspaceID, peerID, target)` for `/v1/peer/{peer_id}/card`.
>   - Keep existing `SceneContext` and `LoreSearch`.
> - Add actor card loading for generated peer-card JSON.
>   - Load accepted Honcho card artifacts from `lore/canon/comics/peer-cards/cards/accepted/*.json`.
>   - Convert `card: []string` into actor card text.
>   - Preserve `lore/actors/*.md` as local overrides for handcrafted test actors.
>   - Do not load non-peer lore as actor cards.
> - Add CLI preview.
>   - `go run ./cmd/cli -context-preview narrator -packet testdata/packets/toy.json -node eastern-hall`
>   - `go run ./cmd/cli -context-preview writer ...`
>   - Output pretty JSON by default; add `-context-text` to print the model-ready text.
> - Wire normal CLI narrator rollout through the assembler.
>   - Replace the current hardcoded `"phase0-cli"` context string with `NarratorContext.RenderText()`.
>   - Keep static tests/fake retrievers available so generation tests do not require Qdrant.
>
> ## Context Semantics
> - `NarratorContext` receives only the selected node, never the full packet tree.
>   - Strip `writer_notes`, `revision_notes`, `invalidation_notes`, and unused branch nodes.
>   - Include active beats, choices, actor needs, current location/time, player decision, recent scenes, relevant lore, actor contexts, and witness policy.
> - `WriterContext` receives the bounded full current packet and revision inputs.
>   - Include latest narrator prose, last user decision, current scene state, selected node, valid actor list, Honcho representations, and lore grouped by kind.
>   - Mark all packet branches as planning artifacts, not canon.
> - `ActorContext` is built only for explicit `node.actor_needs`.
>   - Enforce existing `Phase0ActorCap`.
>   - No all-cast fanout from `present_actors`, peer-card inventory, identity map, or lore hits.
>   - Each actor gets its own card, invocation reason, mode, relevant directional representations, and only scene-valid lore.
> - Witness boundaries are explicit in rendered context.
>   - Actor private interiors may inform the Narrator but are not witnessed memory.
>   - Writer drafts and unused branches must never be sent to Honcho.
>   - Actor contexts should not include another actor’s private interior.
>
> ## Assembly Flow
> - Select node with existing `StoryPacket.Node` / `EntryNode`.
> - Build query text from location, time, selected node title/beats, player decision, present actors, and latest narrator prose.
> - Call bridge `SceneContext` once for recent scenes and narrator/player representation.
> - Call lore retriever once per role:
>   - Narrator: `k=8`, no broad peer-card flood.
>   - Writer: `k=12`, grouped by `kind` for planning breadth.
> - Resolve actor needs:
>   - Actor IDs come only from selected node `actor_needs`.
>   - Actor card source order: Honcho card if present, local accepted peer-card JSON, then `lore/actors/*.md`.
>   - Missing card for an explicit actor need is a hard error.
> - For each actor need, fetch:
>   - actor -> `sans-nom` representation
>   - actor -> each `need.targets` representation, capped at 3 targets
> - Apply budgets before render:
>   - recent scenes: 3 entries, 600 chars each
>   - lore hits: 800 chars each
>   - representations: 1000 chars each
>   - actor card: max 40 facts or equivalent text
>   - total rendered context soft cap: 12k chars narrator, 18k chars writer
> - Add `Warnings []string` when content is truncated, a target representation is unavailable, or a fallback card source is used.
>
> ## Interfaces And Rendering
> - `NarratorContext.RenderText()` sections:
>   - role boundary
>   - current scene state
>   - player decision
>   - selected node
>   - actor contexts
>   - lore references grouped by kind
>   - recent witnessed canon
>   - memory and witness rules
> - `WriterContext.RenderText()` sections:
>   - role boundary
>   - current packet summary/full bounded packet
>   - latest rollout and decision
>   - planning constraints
>   - lore references grouped by kind
>   - actor/card availability
>   - invalidation/revision notes
> - Rendered text is deterministic for tests:
>   - stable actor ordering
>   - stable lore ordering by score then `doc_id`
>   - stable warning ordering
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit tests for assembler behavior:
>   - narrator context excludes unused packet branches and `writer_notes`
>   - writer context includes the full bounded packet and revision notes
>   - no all-cast fanout when many peer cards exist
>   - explicit actor needs are capped and missing actor cards fail
>   - actor target representations are capped and directional
>   - lore hits are deduplicated, sorted, grouped, and truncated
>   - warnings appear for truncation/fallbacks
> - Go bridge tests:
>   - `Representation` posts expected JSON
>   - `GetCard` sends workspace/target query and decodes facts
> - CLI tests or smoke checks:
>   - `go run ./cmd/cli -context-preview narrator -packet testdata/packets/toy.json`
>   - `go run ./cmd/cli -context-preview writer -packet testdata/packets/toy.json -context-text`
>   - normal toy rollout still works and uses assembled narrator context
> - Full verification:
>   - `go test ./...`
>   - `uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q`
>   - with sidecar/Qdrant running, preview includes relevant lore for `Lothar is Steelhead` style probes when the packet text asks for it.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - This phase builds and wires context assembly; it does not create the first-turn seed loop yet.
> - Runtime context preview requires the bridge sidecar and Qdrant for live lore retrieval.
> - Honcho remains the authority for evolved representations; local peer-card JSON is only a fallback/base-card source.
> - Non-peer lore is searchable reference material, never actor material.
> - Writer/Narrator prompt quality iteration comes after this, once preview output is inspectable.
</details>

I have the core shape. One last lookup: how `SceneContext` currently fills peer cards and representations, because that determines whether the assembler should call one bridge endpoint or several.

>   - `go run ./cmd/cli -context-preview writer ...`
>   - Output pretty JSON by default; add `-context-text` to print the model-ready text.
> - Wire normal CLI narrator rollout through the assembler.
>   - Replace the current hardcoded `"phase0-cli"` context string with `NarratorContext.RenderText()`.
>   - Keep static tests/fake retrievers available so generation tests do not require Qdrant.
>
> ## Context Semantics
> - `NarratorContext` receives only the selected node, never the full packet tree.
>   - Strip `writer_notes`, `revision_notes`, `invalidation_notes`, and unused branch nodes.
>   - Include active beats, choices, actor needs, current location/time, player decision, recent scenes, relevant lore, actor contexts, and witness policy.
> - `WriterContext` receives the bounded full current packet and revision inputs.
>   - Include latest narrator prose, last user decision, current scene state, selected node, valid actor list, Honcho representations, and lore grouped by kind.
>   - Mark all packet branches as planning artifacts, not canon.
> - `ActorContext` is built only for explicit `node.actor_needs`.
>   - Enforce existing `Phase0ActorCap`.
>   - No all-cast fanout from `present_actors`, peer-card inventory, identity map, or lore hits.
>   - Each actor gets its own card, invocation reason, mode, relevant directional representations, and only scene-valid lore.
> - Witness boundaries are explicit in rendered context.
>   - Actor private interiors may inform the Narrator but are not witnessed memory.
>   - Writer drafts and unused branches must never be sent to Honcho.
>   - Actor contexts should not include another actor’s private interior.
>
> ## Assembly Flow
> - Select node with existing `StoryPacket.Node` / `EntryNode`.
> - Build query text from location, time, selected node title/beats, player decision, present actors, and latest narrator prose.
> - Call bridge `SceneContext` once for recent scenes and narrator/player representation.
> - Call lore retriever once per role:
>   - Narrator: `k=8`, no broad peer-card flood.
>   - Writer: `k=12`, grouped by `kind` for planning breadth.
> - Resolve actor needs:
>   - Actor IDs come only from selected node `actor_needs`.
>   - Actor card source order: Honcho card if present, local accepted peer-card JSON, then `lore/actors/*.md`.
>   - Missing card for an explicit actor need is a hard error.
> - For each actor need, fetch:
>   - actor -> `sans-nom` representation
>   - actor -> each `need.targets` representation, capped at 3 targets
> - Apply budgets before render:
>   - recent scenes: 3 entries, 600 chars each
>   - lore hits: 800 chars each
>   - representations: 1000 chars each
>   - actor card: max 40 facts or equivalent text
>   - total rendered context soft cap: 12k chars narrator, 18k chars writer
> - Add `Warnings []string` when content is truncated, a target representation is unavailable, or a fallback card source is used.
>
> ## Interfaces And Rendering
> - `NarratorContext.RenderText()` sections:
>   - role boundary
>   - current scene state
>   - player decision
>   - selected node
>   - actor contexts
>   - lore references grouped by kind
>   - recent witnessed canon
>   - memory and witness rules
> - `WriterContext.RenderText()` sections:
>   - role boundary
>   - current packet summary/full bounded packet
>   - latest rollout and decision
>   - planning constraints
>   - lore references grouped by kind
>   - actor/card availability
>   - invalidation/revision notes
> - Rendered text is deterministic for tests:
>   - stable actor ordering
>   - stable lore ordering by score then `doc_id`
>   - stable warning ordering
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit tests for assembler behavior:
>   - narrator context excludes unused packet branches and `writer_notes`
>   - writer context includes the full bounded packet and revision notes
>   - no all-cast fanout when many peer cards exist
>   - explicit actor needs are capped and missing actor cards fail
>   - actor target representations are capped and directional
>   - lore hits are deduplicated, sorted, grouped, and truncated
>   - warnings appear for truncation/fallbacks
> - Go bridge tests:
>   - `Representation` posts expected JSON
>   - `GetCard` sends workspace/target query and decodes facts
> - CLI tests or smoke checks:
>   - `go run ./cmd/cli -context-preview narrator -packet testdata/packets/toy.json`
>   - `go run ./cmd/cli -context-preview writer -packet testdata/packets/toy.json -context-text`
>   - normal toy rollout still works and uses assembled narrator context
> - Full verification:
>   - `go test ./...`
>   - `uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q`
>   - with sidecar/Qdrant running, preview includes relevant lore for `Lothar is Steelhead` style probes when the packet text asks for it.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - This phase builds and wires context assembly; it does not create the first-turn seed loop yet.
> - Runtime context preview requires the bridge sidecar and Qdrant for live lore retrieval.
> - Honcho remains the authority for evolved representations; local peer-card JSON is only a fallback/base-card source.
> - Non-peer lore is searchable reference material, never actor material.
> - Writer/Narrator prompt quality iteration comes after this, once preview output is inspectable.

> # Phase 2 Plan: Context Diet + First Playable Writer/Narrator Loop
>
> ## Summary
> Build the first playable CLI loop on top of the Phase 1c context assembler, but first tighten context budgets so the Writer does not receive a full peer-card inventory. The target is a small live vertical slice: seed an opening packet, roll out narrator prose, accept choices/free text, commit witnessed canon, and refresh the next bounded `StoryPacket`.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a context cleanup pass in `internal/contextbundle`.
>   - Replace full Writer actor-card inventory with compact `ActorManifest`: explicit scene actors, likely slice actors, and retrieved/referenced actor IDs only.
>   - Keep full card facts only for explicit actor needs; for other available actors include `peer_id`, display name, and one-line role summary.
>   - Add hard render caps after section rendering so narrator/writer previews stay below configured budgets instead of only warning.
> - Add a model runtime abstraction.
>   - Keep `prompt.Runner`, but add a Codex OAuth runner using existing `internal/codexoauth` with default `gpt-5.5`, `reasoning.effort=medium`, `service_tier=priority`.
>   - Default live Writer/Narrator/Actor roles to Codex OAuth; keep `claude -p` behind an explicit flag/env fallback.
>   - Add JSON-schema response mode for Writer packets and Narrator drafts when using Codex OAuth.
> - Wire Writer to real context.
>   - Change the Writer planner interface to accept `WriterContext.RenderText()` or a `WriterInput` containing packet, decision, and assembled context.
>   - Update `WriterPrompt` so it no longer gets only raw packet JSON; it receives role boundary, latest rollout, decision, lore, actor manifest, revision notes, and packet schema rules.
>   - `-refresh-writer` should assemble Writer context first, call the live Writer, validate the returned `StoryPacket`, and only replace the current packet if validation passes.
> - Add first-turn story seeding.
>   - Add `-seed-story` CLI mode that builds an opening `StoryPacket` for the Phase 1 childhood slice.
>   - Use a two-role seed loop: `Scenarist` proposes a 3-5 node packet; `NerdVerifier` checks lore fit, slice boundaries, schema validity, no council mode, no forbidden Phase 1 events, and no actor fanout.
>   - Save no files by default; print the packet JSON to stdout. Add `-seed-output path` only if explicitly supplied.
> - Add interactive CLI loop.
>   - Add `-play` mode: seed or load packet, render current node, show choices, read `choice id` or free text, commit via bridge when `-commit` is set, then refresh the next packet in the background.
>   - Preserve non-mutating dry mode by default: without `-commit`, print the prepared commit but do not call Honcho.
>   - Support `-turns N` for automated toy playthrough smoke tests.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit tests:
>   - Writer context no longer includes every accepted peer card.
>   - Explicit actor needs still receive full cards and missing cards still fail.
>   - Rendered contexts enforce hard caps deterministically.
>   - Codex OAuth runner builds the expected Responses body: model, reasoning effort, service tier, JSON schema.
>   - Writer refresh uses assembled context and rejects invalid packets without replacing the current packet.
>   - Seeder verifier rejects council mode, over-cap actor needs, Phase 1 forbidden events, and malformed packets.
> - CLI/integration tests:
>   - `go test ./...`
>   - `uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q`
>   - `go run ./cmd/cli -context-preview writer -packet testdata/packets/toy.json -context-text` stays under budget.
>   - `go run ./cmd/cli -seed-story` returns a valid 3-5 node `StoryPacket`.
>   - `go run ./cmd/cli -play -packet testdata/packets/toy.json -turns 3` runs without Honcho commit.
>   - With sidecar/Qdrant running: `go run ./cmd/cli -play -seed-story -turns 3 -commit` commits witnessed canon only.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - This phase remains CLI-only; no UI or streaming yet.
> - Codex OAuth `gpt-5.5` is the default live model path; Claude stays available but not default.
> - Service tier value for direct Codex OAuth calls is `priority`.
> - Honcho writes remain opt-in via `-commit`; dry mode stays the default for development.
> - The seed story targets the Phase 1 childhood slice at Aghora's compound, not the full game.
</details>

> how do i play?

From repo root:

```bash
cd /Users/vincent/dev/sans-nom
go run ./cmd/cli -seed-story -play
```

It will generate an opening packet, narrate turn 1, print choices, then prompt:

```text
choice id or free text>
```

You can type either:

```text
1
```

or the exact choice id, like:

```text
choice_confess_hand
```

Useful variants:

```bash
# See machine-readable turn/choice trace too
go run ./cmd/cli -seed-story -play -play-trace-jsonl

# Fast deterministic local toy, no live model
go run ./cmd/cli -packet testdata/packets/toy.json -play -model-backend static

# Let free-text drive writer refresh after a turn
go run ./cmd/cli -seed-story -play -refresh-writer
```

By default it is dry-run: it prints `Commit prepared` but does not write to Honcho. Use `-commit` only when the bridge/sidecar is up and you actually want scene memory writes.

> Plan
>
> # Plan: Durable Story Seed, Workspace, And Resume Loop
>
> ## Summary
> Replace the current one-prompt `-seed-story` with a real story-initialization pipeline. The first turn will generate a durable original Story Bible plus the first `StoryPacket`, seed the story’s local data directory, create the story Qdrant collection, seed a Honcho workspace, and then let the Narrator produce a longer classic opening that establishes world, player character, connection, law, pressure, and choices.
>
> The Metabarons corpus remains source teaching material. Deep facts like Bushitaka are not copied literally; the seed must create original equivalent laws with the same structural force and store them as binding story doctrine.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a story workspace layer:
>   - New story dir: `data/stories/<story_id>/`.
>   - Persist `state.json`, `bible.json`, `packets/*.json`, `turns.jsonl`, `model-runs/*.json`, `index/documents.jsonl`, and `index/manifest.json`.
>   - Add `data/stories/` to `.gitignore`; test fixtures stay under `testdata/`.
> - Add a `StoryBible` runtime artifact:
>   - Contains title, premise, player character, world basics, original story laws, factions, core relationships, tone doctrine, source-lore influence refs, forbidden literal canon terms, and resume metadata.
>   - Requires at least one original “gravity law” derived from Bushitaka-like source structure: profound, binding, not merely cruel, and enforced by world reaction rather than system blocking.
>   - Requires first-turn exposition intent: world, player identity, player-world connection, active taboo/law, immediate pressure, and choices.
> - Change first-turn generation:
>   - `-seed-story` becomes a multi-artifact seed loop: Scenarist returns `StoryBible + StoryPacket`; Verifier rejects weak world setup, missing original law, literal canon import, no player-world connection, or too-short opening structure.
>   - The first entry node should be richer than later nodes: multiple beats and 2-4 choices, enough for the Narrator to produce a long opening.
>   - Writer/Narrator contexts include the Story Bible as binding doctrine, separate from creative influence lore.
> - Add per-story persistence and resume:
>   - `-story-id <id> -play` loads `data/stories/<id>/state.json`.
>   - `-seed-story -story-id <id>` creates a new story id if omitted, or fails if the id already exists unless an explicit replace flag is provided.
>   - After each rollout, save the selected node, player decision, narrator prose, commit preview/result, current packet, and next node/packet pointer.
> - Add per-story retrieval and external system seeding:
>   - Keep global `sans_nom_lore` read-only for source inspiration.
>   - Create a story collection named `sans_nom_story_<story_id>` containing generated bible sections, original story laws, generated peer/card facts, narrator prose, committed turn summaries, and current packet summaries.
>   - Runtime lore retrieval queries both collections: source lore for influence, story collection for canon/cohesion.
>   - Extend bridge search with a `collection` selector and add a story-index endpoint/command for embedding story documents with Voyage.
>   - `-seed-story` creates the story Qdrant collection and Honcho workspace/cards by default for live mode; static tests use fake/in-memory paths.
> - Seed Honcho workspace:
>   - Workspace id defaults to `story_id`.
>   - Seed base cards for `narrator`, `creative-writer`, and player peer `sans-nom`, including the story’s original laws and boundaries.
>   - Do not commit turn canon unless the play path uses `-commit`; workspace/card creation is part of story initialization.
>
> ## CLI And Interfaces
> - CLI flags:
>   - `-story-id <id>`: create/resume story.
>   - `-story-root data/stories`: override local story storage.
>   - `-global-lore-collection sans_nom_lore`: source lore collection.
>   - `-story-collection <name>`: optional override; default derived from story id.
>   - `-replace-story`: explicitly recreate an existing story dir/collection/workspace seed.
> - Go types:
>   - Add `internal/story` package with `StoryState`, `StoryBible`, `StoryWorkspace`, and `StoryIndexDocument`.
>   - Extend `contextbundle.BuildRequest` with optional `StoryBible` and story collection config.
>   - Extend `bridge.LoreSearchRequest` with `Collection`.
> - Bridge:
>   - Add collection-aware lore search.
>   - Add story index ingestion using the existing Voyage/Qdrant helpers and deterministic fake embeddings for tests.
>   - Keep global lore-index behavior unchanged.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit tests:
>   - Story Bible validation rejects missing original law, missing player-world connection, literal Metabarons canon terms, and weak first-turn exposition.
>   - Story workspace creates stable `story_id`, writes all required files, and resumes current packet/node.
>   - Context assembly includes Story Bible doctrine and keeps source lore under influence references.
>   - Bridge collection selector queries requested collection and story indexing supports fake embeddings.
> - CLI tests:
>   - Static `-seed-story -story-id test-id -play -model-backend static` creates `data/stories/test-id`, writes state, and can resume with `-story-id test-id -play`.
>   - Existing choice e2e still passes.
>   - Free text without refresh still stops clearly; with refresh it updates state.
> - Live gated smoke:
>   - `SANS_NOM_E2E_LIVE=1 go test ./cmd/cli -run TestLiveStorySeedWorkspaceResumeE2E -count=1 -timeout=8m`.
>   - Assert story dir exists, Qdrant story collection receives story docs, Honcho cards are seeded, first narrator turn is long, choices are present, and resume continues from saved state.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - “Bushitaka law” means an original equivalent law with the same authorial gravity, not the literal canon Bushitaka.
> - Runtime story dirs are local generated state and should not be committed by default.
> - Live `-seed-story` requires Voyage, Qdrant, Honcho, and Codex OAuth to be configured; static mode remains available for tests.
> - Scene memory commits remain controlled by `-commit`; story initialization still writes files, story vectors, and Honcho seed cards.
</details>

Good, that locks the big semantic point: Bushitaka is not copied; the seed creates an original load-bearing law with equivalent structural gravity, and stores it as story bible doctrine for all future Writer/Narrator turns. One storage decision remains around retrieval layout.

>   - New story dir: `data/stories/<story_id>/`.
>   - Persist `state.json`, `bible.json`, `packets/*.json`, `turns.jsonl`, `model-runs/*.json`, `index/documents.jsonl`, and `index/manifest.json`.
>   - Add `data/stories/` to `.gitignore`; test fixtures stay under `testdata/`.
> - Add a `StoryBible` runtime artifact:
>   - Contains title, premise, player character, world basics, original story laws, factions, core relationships, tone doctrine, source-lore influence refs, forbidden literal canon terms, and resume metadata.
>   - Requires at least one original “gravity law” derived from Bushitaka-like source structure: profound, binding, not merely cruel, and enforced by world reaction rather than system blocking.
>   - Requires first-turn exposition intent: world, player identity, player-world connection, active taboo/law, immediate pressure, and choices.
> - Change first-turn generation:
>   - `-seed-story` becomes a multi-artifact seed loop: Scenarist returns `StoryBible + StoryPacket`; Verifier rejects weak world setup, missing original law, literal canon import, no player-world connection, or too-short opening structure.
>   - The first entry node should be richer than later nodes: multiple beats and 2-4 choices, enough for the Narrator to produce a long opening.
>   - Writer/Narrator contexts include the Story Bible as binding doctrine, separate from creative influence lore.
> - Add per-story persistence and resume:
>   - `-story-id <id> -play` loads `data/stories/<id>/state.json`.
>   - `-seed-story -story-id <id>` creates a new story id if omitted, or fails if the id already exists unless an explicit replace flag is provided.
>   - After each rollout, save the selected node, player decision, narrator prose, commit preview/result, current packet, and next node/packet pointer.
> - Add per-story retrieval and external system seeding:
>   - Keep global `sans_nom_lore` read-only for source inspiration.
>   - Create a story collection named `sans_nom_story_<story_id>` containing generated bible sections, original story laws, generated peer/card facts, narrator prose, committed turn summaries, and current packet summaries.
>   - Runtime lore retrieval queries both collections: source lore for influence, story collection for canon/cohesion.
>   - Extend bridge search with a `collection` selector and add a story-index endpoint/command for embedding story documents with Voyage.
>   - `-seed-story` creates the story Qdrant collection and Honcho workspace/cards by default for live mode; static tests use fake/in-memory paths.
> - Seed Honcho workspace:
>   - Workspace id defaults to `story_id`.
>   - Seed base cards for `narrator`, `creative-writer`, and player peer `sans-nom`, including the story’s original laws and boundaries.
>   - Do not commit turn canon unless the play path uses `-commit`; workspace/card creation is part of story initialization.
>
> ## CLI And Interfaces
> - CLI flags:
>   - `-story-id <id>`: create/resume story.
>   - `-story-root data/stories`: override local story storage.
>   - `-global-lore-collection sans_nom_lore`: source lore collection.
>   - `-story-collection <name>`: optional override; default derived from story id.
>   - `-replace-story`: explicitly recreate an existing story dir/collection/workspace seed.
> - Go types:
>   - Add `internal/story` package with `StoryState`, `StoryBible`, `StoryWorkspace`, and `StoryIndexDocument`.
>   - Extend `contextbundle.BuildRequest` with optional `StoryBible` and story collection config.
>   - Extend `bridge.LoreSearchRequest` with `Collection`.
> - Bridge:
>   - Add collection-aware lore search.
>   - Add story index ingestion using the existing Voyage/Qdrant helpers and deterministic fake embeddings for tests.
>   - Keep global lore-index behavior unchanged.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit tests:
>   - Story Bible validation rejects missing original law, missing player-world connection, literal Metabarons canon terms, and weak first-turn exposition.
>   - Story workspace creates stable `story_id`, writes all required files, and resumes current packet/node.
>   - Context assembly includes Story Bible doctrine and keeps source lore under influence references.
>   - Bridge collection selector queries requested collection and story indexing supports fake embeddings.
> - CLI tests:
>   - Static `-seed-story -story-id test-id -play -model-backend static` creates `data/stories/test-id`, writes state, and can resume with `-story-id test-id -play`.
>   - Existing choice e2e still passes.
>   - Free text without refresh still stops clearly; with refresh it updates state.
> - Live gated smoke:
>   - `SANS_NOM_E2E_LIVE=1 go test ./cmd/cli -run TestLiveStorySeedWorkspaceResumeE2E -count=1 -timeout=8m`.
>   - Assert story dir exists, Qdrant story collection receives story docs, Honcho cards are seeded, first narrator turn is long, choices are present, and resume continues from saved state.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - “Bushitaka law” means an original equivalent law with the same authorial gravity, not the literal canon Bushitaka.
> - Runtime story dirs are local generated state and should not be committed by default.
> - Live `-seed-story` requires Voyage, Qdrant, Honcho, and Codex OAuth to be configured; static mode remains available for tests.
> - Scene memory commits remain controlled by `-commit`; story initialization still writes files, story vectors, and Honcho seed cards.
