> # Plan: Agentic Scenarist Support For Writer Refresh
>
> ## Summary
> Add a bounded idea-agent phase before the Creative Writer returns a revised `StoryPacket`. The Writer will ask for help on specific story problems, run 0-3 focused Scenarist agents, then integrate their JSON memos into the final Writer prompt. Scenarist output stays planning-only: it is never Honcho canon, never story-index canon, and never player-facing prose.
>
> Use `_test.sh` only as the prototype reference. Do not call it from runtime. Recreate its Claude-compatible provider behavior in Go, including provider-prefixed env loading from `.env` / `.env.example`.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add `internal/scenarist` with:
>   - `TopicRequestSet`: max 3 requests, each requiring `topic_id`, `story_problem`, `desired_use`, `constraints`, `avoid`, `lore_influence_refs`, and `max_ideas`.
>   - `Memo`: strict JSON with `topic_id`, `best_ideas`, `story_law_pressure`, `character_pressure`, `choice_shapes`, `risks`, and `do_not_use`.
>   - Validators rejecting vague brainstorms, empty constraints, literal canon terms, over-cap ideas, and generic “cool sci-fi” output.
> - Add a `writer.AgenticPlanner` wrapper:
>   - First call asks the Writer to produce focused scenarist topic requests from `WriterContext`.
>   - Runs Scenarist agents concurrently with bounded timeout.
>   - Final Writer call receives the original context plus accepted memos and returns the normal `StoryPacket`.
>   - If topic selection returns zero valid requests, it falls back to normal Writer planning.
> - Add prompt templates:
>   - `WriterTopicPrompt`: asks only for specific help requests, not story prose.
>   - `ScenaristPrompt`: rooted in passion for Metabarons as philosophical/entertainment craft influence, but forbids copying names, events, factions, or mechanics.
>   - `WriterPromptWithMemos`: tells Writer that memos are optional inspiration, not canon and not requirements.
> - Add a Claude-compatible provider runner:
>   - Loads env vars by provider prefix, e.g. `ZAI__ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` -> `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`.
>   - Uses `claude --bare --system-prompt ... -p ... --model ... --json-schema ...`.
>   - Default provider from `SANS_NOM_SCENARIST_PROVIDER`, CLI override `-scenarist-provider`.
>   - Default model from provider env / `-scenarist-model`.
> - Add optional read-tools mode:
>   - Default: curated context only.
>   - `-scenarist-tools` enables read-only Claude tools with `--bare`, `--permission-mode plan`, `--add-dir lore`, and read-only tool allowlist.
>   - Tool prompt includes path map for `lore/canon/wiki/lore.md`, `lore/canon/links/matrix.md`, `lore/canon/index/documents.jsonl`, accepted peer cards, and current story index.
> - CLI flags:
>   - `-writer-scenarists N`, default `3` for live `-refresh-writer`, `0` disables.
>   - `-scenarist-provider ZAI|MINIMAX|XIAOMI`, default env-driven.
>   - `-scenarist-model <model>`, optional.
>   - `-scenarist-tools`, default false.
>   - Static backend uses fake scenarist memos only in tests; no live provider calls.
> - Persist audit artifacts under the story workspace:
>   - `model-runs/writer-scenarists/<turn>-topics.json`
>   - `model-runs/writer-scenarists/<turn>-memo-<topic_id>.json`
>   - `model-runs/writer-scenarists/<turn>-final-writer-input.json`
>   - These artifacts are planning traces only and are not indexed into story canon.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit tests:
>   - Topic request validation rejects vague, over-cap, unconstrained, and literal-canon requests.
>   - Scenarist memo validation rejects unsupported/random ideas and literal-canon imports.
>   - Provider env loader maps `ZAI__*` variables correctly and fails clearly on missing token/base URL/model.
>   - Agentic planner calls topic selection, runs bounded fake scenarists, and passes memos into final Writer prompt.
>   - Agentic planner falls back cleanly when no valid topics are requested.
>   - Tool-enabled runner builds read-only Claude CLI args and never enables edit/write tools.
> - Regression tests:
>   - Scenarist memos are not included in Honcho commits.
>   - Scenarist memos are not added to story index documents.
>   - Existing `writer.StaticPlanner`, normal Writer refresh, and static CLI play still pass unchanged.
> - Smoke tests:
>   - `go test ./...`
>   - `uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q`
>   - Manual provider smoke: run `-refresh-writer -writer-scenarists 2 -scenarist-provider ZAI` on a saved story and verify topic/memo artifacts plus a valid revised `StoryPacket`.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - First implementation uses Claude-compatible providers, not Codex OAuth, for scenarist agents.
> - Default mode is curated context only; read-tools mode is explicit because it is slower and more variable.
> - Scenarists advise on focused topics; only the Creative Writer may decide what enters the `StoryPacket`.
> - Scenarist ideas are allowed to be vivid and strange, but must be shaped by the current Story Bible, current packet, player decision, and source-lore influence refs.
> - `_test.sh` remains a rough dev reference unless separately promoted into a maintained smoke script.
</details>

> # Plan: Free-Form Scenarist Material For Agentic Writer
>
> ## Summary
> Make Writer refresh more agentic by adding a “scenarist workshop” phase. The Writer first asks for focused creative help, the runtime launches Scenarist agents, each Scenarist writes an unconstrained free-form text artifact, and the final Writer call receives only a compact manifest of output file paths. The Writer uses read-only tools to inspect those files as needed, keeping its initial context small while preserving creative breadth.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add `internal/scenarist` as a workshop layer:
>   - Writer produces a strict `ScenaristBriefSet` with up to 3 briefs: topic, story problem, current pressure, desired kind of help, hard boundaries, and relevant lore/story paths.
>   - Scenarist output itself is free-form text, not JSON and not schema-constrained.
>   - Each output is written atomically under `data/stories/<story_id>/model-runs/scenarists/<turn>/<topic_id>.md`.
> - Scenarist instructions:
>   - Root the agent in passion for Metabarons-style craft: philosophical pressure, body/law/taboo, spectacle, entertainment value, and durable questions.
>   - Require originality: no copied canon names, events, factions, dynasty mechanics, council mode, or direct equivalents.
>   - Encourage vivid, useful material: world laws, character contradictions, scene engines, choice pressures, images, taboos, rituals, possible reversals.
>   - Do not ask for final `StoryPacket`, narrator prose, or structured output.
> - Writer integration:
>   - Final Writer prompt gets the Story Bible, reduced direct lore context, current packet state, and a “Scenarist Material Manifest” listing topic ids and file paths only.
>   - Final Writer runner gets read-only access to the scenarist output folder and may read files selectively.
>   - Writer remains responsible for producing the only structured `StoryPacket`; scenarist files are inspiration, not requirements.
> - Runtime/backend:
>   - Implement a Claude-compatible provider runner based on `_test.sh`: provider-prefixed env loading such as `ZAI__ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL -> ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `claude --bare`, provider/model flags, and clear missing-env errors.
>   - Scenarists use Claude-compatible providers first; default from `SANS_NOM_SCENARIST_PROVIDER`, override with `-scenarist-provider`.
>   - Add `-writer-scenarists N` default `3` for live `-refresh-writer`, `0` disables.
>   - Add `-scenarist-model`, `-scenarist-tools`, and `-scenarist-output-root` optional flags.
> - Tool/read policy:
>   - Scenarists default to curated context plus path pointers; optional `-scenarist-tools` gives read-only lore access.
>   - Final Writer always gets read-only access to the scenarist output folder when scenarists ran.
>   - Scenarist artifacts are planning material only: do not commit to Honcho, do not index as story canon, do not surface to Narrator.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit tests:
>   - Brief generation caps at 3 topics and rejects empty/vague briefs.
>   - Provider env loader maps provider-prefixed variables and fails on missing base URL/token/model.
>   - Free-form scenarist outputs are written atomically and recorded in a manifest.
>   - Agentic Writer passes only paths, not raw scenarist text, into the final Writer prompt.
>   - Final Writer runner receives read-only access to the scenarist output folder.
> - Regression tests:
>   - Scenarist outputs are not included in Honcho commits.
>   - Scenarist outputs are not indexed into story canon.
>   - `-writer-scenarists 0` preserves existing Writer behavior.
>   - Static backend remains deterministic and does not call live providers.
> - Smoke tests:
>   - `go test ./...`
>   - `uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q`
>   - Manual: `go run ./cmd/cli -story-id <id> -play -refresh-writer -writer-scenarists 2 -scenarist-provider ZAI`
>
> ## Assumptions
> - Scenarist output should maximize creative usefulness, so no JSON schema is imposed on the output files.
> - Control comes from the Writer’s briefs, story/lore boundaries, file budgets, and final Writer responsibility.
> - Direct source-lore in Writer context is reduced when scenarist material exists; Story Bible remains binding.
> - `_test.sh` stays a prototype/reference unless separately converted into a maintained smoke helper.
</details>

That changes the architecture in a good way: scenarists should be creative context compressors, not schema-constrained mini-writers. The control should move into topic framing, budget, and Writer integration rules, not output format validation.

>   - Add `-scenarist-model`, `-scenarist-tools`, and `-scenarist-output-root` optional flags.
> - Tool/read policy:

Changes:
- Default scenarist provider pool is now `ZAI,MINIMAX,XIAOMI`.
- Pool filters out providers that do not have usable env values, so placeholder `***` providers do not break the tool.
- `call_scenarists` max parallelism is now based on usable provider count unless capped by `-writer-scenarists`.
- Provider pool now has per-provider leases, so one provider cannot run more than one scenarist call concurrently.
- Added tests for default provider names, usable-provider filtering, round-robin available slots, busy-provider waiting, and tool parallelism.

> # Fullscreen CLI Menu
>
> ## Summary
> Add a fullscreen Bubble Tea TUI when the CLI is launched with no flags: `go run ./cmd/cli`. The menu shows `New Story`, `Resume Story`, and `Exit`. Any existing flag-based invocation keeps the current behavior unchanged.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a small TUI layer using Charm libraries: Bubble Tea with alt-screen fullscreen mode, Bubbles list for menus, and Lip Gloss for minimal styling.
> - Entry behavior:
>   - If `len(os.Args) == 1`, launch the TUI.
>   - If any flag is present, keep the existing flag-driven CLI path exactly as it works now.
> - Main menu:
>   - `New Story`: call the existing seed workspace flow with current default/env config, then enter the existing interactive `runPlay` loop.
>   - `Resume Story`: open a story picker populated from `data/stories` or the configured story root, then enter `runPlay` at the saved packet/node.
>   - `Exit`: quit cleanly with status `0`.
> - Resume picker:
>   - List only valid story dirs with readable `state.json` and `bible.json`.
>   - Display title when available, otherwise story id.
>   - Include story id, latest turn, and updated timestamp as secondary text.
>   - Sort by `UpdatedAt` descending, newest first.
>   - If no stories exist, show an empty state with `Back` and `Exit`.
> - Keep the TUI as a dispatcher only: gameplay, story seeding, resume loading, bridge/Qdrant/Honcho behavior, and dry/commit defaults stay owned by existing CLI functions.
>
> ## Interfaces
> - Add an internal TUI package or small CLI-local TUI module with:
>   - `RunMainMenu(ctx, deps/options) (Action, error)`
>   - `ActionNewStory`, `ActionResumeStory{StoryID}`, `ActionExit`
>   - `ListStorySummaries(root string) ([]StorySummary, error)`
> - Reuse existing `story.LoadWorkspace`, `Workspace.LoadBible`, and `Workspace.LoadPacket`.
> - TUI selection should return an action; `main()` performs the action using existing `seedStoryWorkspace` and `runPlay` code paths.

> ## Assumptions

> # Fullscreen CLI Menu With Reusable App Actions
>
> ## Summary
> Add a fullscreen Bubble Tea TUI when the CLI is launched with no flags: `go run ./cmd/cli`. The menu shows `New Story`, `Resume Story`, and `Exit`. Structure the work so future GUIs, such as a web UI, can reuse the same story actions instead of duplicating CLI/TUI logic.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a small reusable application layer for GUI-facing actions:
>   - `NewStory(ctx, options) -> StorySession`
>   - `ListStories(root) -> []StorySummary`
>   - `ResumeStory(ctx, storyID, options) -> StorySession`
>   - This layer wraps existing `seedStoryWorkspace`, `story.LoadWorkspace`, bible/packet loading, and play config assembly.
> - Add a Bubble Tea TUI as a thin frontend over that app layer:
>   - `New Story`: create a durable story with existing default/env config, then enter the current interactive play loop.
>   - `Resume Story`: open a story picker, load the selected story, then enter the current interactive play loop.
>   - `Exit`: quit with status `0`.
> - Preserve existing CLI behavior:
>   - If `len(os.Args) == 1`, launch TUI.
>   - If any flag is present, use the current flag-based flow unchanged.
> - Resume picker:
>   - List only valid story dirs with readable `state.json` and `bible.json`.
>   - Display title when available, otherwise story id.
>   - Show story id, latest turn, and updated timestamp as secondary text.
>   - Sort by `UpdatedAt` descending.
>   - If no stories exist, show `Back` and `Exit`.
> - Keep gameplay rendering and input in the existing CLI play loop for this phase; the TUI is only the entry/menu layer.
>
> ## Interfaces
> - Introduce GUI-safe types that do not depend on Bubble Tea:
>   - `StorySummary`
>   - `StorySession`
>   - `StoryActionOptions`
> - The TUI returns an action/result; `main()` dispatches it through the reusable app layer.
> - Avoid embedding terminal-specific assumptions in the app layer so a future web UI can call the same story list/create/resume functions.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit-test app layer:

>   - stories sort newest first;
>   - labels fall back to story id;

> ## Assumptions
> - Bubble Tea is the TUI dependency.
> - “Fullscreen” means Bubble Tea alt-screen mode.

`SIDECAR_TOKEN=dev-sidecar-token`

Used by the Python bridge for auth. If set, protected bridge endpoints require:

```http
Authorization: Bearer dev-sidecar-token
```

The Go CLI reads the same env and sends it when calling the bridge. `/v1/health` is open; scene, lore, card, repr, commit, story index endpoints are protected.

`SANS_NOM_MODEL=sonnet`

Used only by the Claude CLI runner. It becomes:

```sh
claude --model sonnet ...
```

In the current default path, the CLI defaults to Codex OAuth (`gpt-5.5`), so this is only relevant when using `-claude` or `-model-backend claude`.

`SANS_NOM_MODEL_EFFORT=medium`

Also Claude-only. It becomes:

```sh
claude ... --effort medium
```

Same caveat: ignored on the normal Codex backend path. Codex uses separate envs like `SANS_NOM_CODEX_MODEL`, `SANS_NOM_CODEX_EFFORT`, and `SANS_NOM_CODEX_OAUTH_SERVICE_TIER`.

Fixed. The problem was not the sidecar startup itself.

`tmp/bridge-sidecar.log` showed the bridge started and `/v1/health` returned `200 OK`, but the Go client decoded health into `map[string]string`. The bridge health payload includes booleans like `honcho_live` and `voyage_configured`, so decoding failed, the launcher thought health never became ready, then killed the sidecar.

Changed:

- [internal/bridge/client.go](./internal/bridge/client.go): health now decodes into `map[string]any`
- [internal/bridge/client_test.go](./internal/bridge/client_test.go): added regression test for mixed string/bool health payload

> I dont see the reasoning and service tiers

<details><summary>1 previous message</summary>

> I’ll trace the request body construction and the final HTTP body mutation, because the runner may set those fields before the client coerces the body.
</details>

They are not in `internal/codexoauth/client.go`; they are added one layer above, in [internal/prompt/codex.go](./internal/prompt/codex.go).

The flow is:

1. [cmd/cli/main.go](./cmd/cli/main.go) builds `prompt.CodexRunner`:

```go
Effort:      "medium"
ServiceTier: "priority"
```

from env/defaults.

2. [internal/prompt/codex.go](./internal/prompt/codex.go) builds the request body:

```go
"reasoning": map[string]any{
    "effort": r.effort(),
},
"service_tier": r.serviceTier(),
```

3. That body is passed to `internal/codexoauth.Client.Create(...)`.

4. `internal/codexoauth/client.go` only coerces backend-specific details:
- force `stream=true`
- force `store=false`
- resolve model
- inject instructions/system prompt
- strip unsupported sampling fields

It does not add reasoning or service tier itself, but it preserves them because `coerceBody` copies all incoming fields before mutating a few specific ones.

So yes, the active request includes them when called through `prompt.CodexRunner`. The lower-level `cmd/codex-responses-json` helper only sends whatever is present in the JSON body you give it; it does not add defaults.

Likely cause: the Codex model call timed out, not the bridge.

Evidence from `tmp/bridge-sidecar.log`:
- bridge started fine
- `/v1/health` returned `200 OK`
- `/v1/scene/context` returned `200 OK`
- `/v1/lore/search` returned `200 OK`
- then the sidecar shut down because the CLI exited

So the failure is after context assembly, during `New Story` seed generation:

`New Story -> generateSeedBundle -> CodexRunner.Run -> 3 minute timeout`

Two things make that likely:

1. Your `.env` currently has:

```env
SANS_NOM_CODEX_EFFORT="xhigh"
SANS_NOM_CODEX_MODEL="gpt-5.5"
SANS_NOM_CODEX_OAUTH_SERVICE_TIER="priority"
```

`xhigh` is too slow/wasteful for seed generation.

2. The runner timeout is currently hardcoded to `3 * time.Minute` in `cmd/cli/main.go`.

Also I see the default in code drifted from `medium` to `xhigh`:

```go
if effort == "" {
    effort = "xhigh"
}
```

That is probably wrong for gameplay.

Recommended fix:
- set default back to `medium`
- remove or change `.env` `SANS_NOM_CODEX_EFFORT="xhigh"` to `medium`
- optionally add clearer error wrapping like `seed scenarist timed out`
- maybe use a longer timeout only for explicitly expensive roles, not default play/seed.

Yes, it is fishy. Root cause found.

The live seed path is accidentally feeding the static Glasswell demo packet into the model.

In [cmd/cli/main.go](./cmd/cli/main.go:501):

```go
packet := seed.DefaultPacket()
writerContext, err := assembler.AssembleWriter(ctx, contextbundle.BuildRequest{Packet: packet})
contextText += "\n\nRuntime lore context:\n" + writerContext.RenderText()
```

And `seed.DefaultPacket()` / `seed.DefaultBible()` are literally the Glasswell/Ila fixture in [internal/seed/seed.go](./internal/seed/seed.go:148):

```go
Title: "The Glasswell Debt"
Name: "Ila Venn"
Location: "Veyr Tidemarket, beneath the Mourning Lantern"
```

So the model is not independently inventing the same story. We are anchoring it with the full example packet, then asking it to create a new seed. It copies/adapts the strongest concrete material in context.

Fix: remove `seed.DefaultPacket()` from live seed context. Static backend can keep it for tests, but live `-seed-story` should get only seed instructions plus source-lore influence snippets, not the Glasswell fixture.

It is unused because it is stale plumbing from the old seed path.

Before the seed leak fix, `newStorySession(...)` passed `cardStore` into `generateSeedBundle(...)`, and seed generation used `contextAssembler(...)`. That assembler could use cards. After the fix, live seed generation only uses:

- `backend`
- `bridgeURL`
- `globalCollection`

via `buildSeedContext(...)` / `seedLoreRetriever(...)`.

So at [cmd/cli/main.go](./cmd/cli/main.go:361), `cardStore` is accepted but never read. The two call sites still pass it at [cmd/cli/main.go](./cmd/cli/main.go:125) and [cmd/cli/main.go](./cmd/cli/main.go:339).

This is not a missed dependency. For seed creation, we probably should not use `cardStore`, because that would pull actor/peer-card material into the first story seed and risks the same kind of contamination we just removed.

Clean fix: remove `cardStore *contextbundle.LocalCardStore` from `newStorySession(...)` and both call sites. Keep `CardStore` on `launcherConfig` because play/context assembly still needs it.

>
> # Admin Visibility + Classified Runtime Logging
>
> ## Summary
> Add a local-first observability layer and a Go admin web UI. The UI launches only with an explicit flag, reads all local app/story stores, tails classified logs, and exposes confirmed control-plane actions for reindexing and runtime inspection. Runtime defaults stay game-first; admin is a separate local operator surface.
>
> ## Key Changes
>
> - Add structured per-story logging under `data/stories/<story_id>/logs/events.jsonl`.
>   - Event envelope: `time`, `level`, `category`, `event`, `story_id`, `turn`, `packet_id`, `node_id`, `run_id`, `message`, `fields`.
>   - Categories: `system`, `story`, `writer`, `narrator`, `actor`, `scenarist`, `model`, `lore`, `bridge`, `honcho`, `qdrant`, `memory`, `control`, `ui`.
>   - Store rich local visibility: prompt names, model backend/model/effort, context sizes, selected choices, retrieval counts/scores, commit summaries, file paths, model-run artifact paths, and errors.
>   - Redact only secrets and auth material: API keys, bearer tokens, OAuth tokens, `.env` values marked secret.
>
> - Replace ad hoc telemetry with a shared Go logging package.
>   - Keep existing `telemetry.Sink` compatible, but route it through the new event writer.
>   - Add story-scoped logger creation in story workspace/session setup.
>   - Log major lifecycle events: story create/resume, seed generation, story index ingest, Honcho card seed, narrator rollout, writer refresh, scenarist tool calls, lore searches, commits, persistence writes, and control-plane actions.
>
> - Add explicit admin web server in Go.
>   - CLI flag: `-admin` starts only the admin server, no play loop.
>   - Optional flags: `-admin-addr 127.0.0.1:8790`, existing `-story-root`, `-bridge-url`.
>   - Bind localhost only by default.
>   - Use Go `net/http` + `html/template`, no JS/frontend build stack for this first slice.
>   - Add a simple HTML UI with tabs: Stories, Story Detail, Logs, Model Runs, Index, Bridge/External, Control.
>
> - Admin read surfaces:
>   - List stories with title, id, turn, updated time, current packet/node, collection names.
>   - Inspect `state.json`, `bible.json`, current/all packets, `turns.jsonl`, `model-runs/`, `index/documents.jsonl`, `index/manifest.json`, and per-story logs.
>   - Show bridge health, Honcho live flag, Voyage config flag, Qdrant URL, and story/global collection names.
>   - Provide raw JSON views plus compact summaries.
>
> - Admin control plane, with confirmation on every mutation:
>   - Rebuild local story index from bible/current packet/turns.
>   - Reingest story index through the bridge.
>   - Refresh current writer packet for a selected story/node.
>   - Recommit a selected turn only if its stored commit is canon-valid.
>   - No destructive delete/reset actions in this pass.
>
> ## Tests
>
> - Go unit tests:
>   - Log event schema, category validation, secret redaction, append/read/tail behavior.
>   - Story logger writes under the correct story directory.
>   - Admin handlers list stories, read files, reject path traversal, filter logs, and render without panics.
>   - Control handlers require confirmation and emit `control` log events.
>   - Existing telemetry lore-search path still emits expected fields.
>
> - Bridge/Python tests remain unchanged unless endpoint shapes are touched.
> - Full verification:
>   - `go test ./...`
>   - `uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q`
>
> ## Assumptions
>
> - Admin UI is local operator tooling, not player UI.
> - `-admin` is explicit; `go run ./cmd/cli` remains the live TUI/game launcher.
> - Per-story JSONL is the durable log source of truth for now; no SQLite.
> - “Everything exposed” means all local runtime stores and safe external status/reads are visible; secrets stay redacted.
> - Control-plane actions are allowed but always localhost-bound and confirmation-gated.
</details>

Good. With Go server + per-story JSONL + control plane, the remaining high-impact choices are safety and launch behavior. These materially affect implementation because admin actions can rewrite indexes, call models, and commit memory.

> starting with no frontend framework isn't a footgun ?

<details><summary>1 previous message</summary>

> I’ll sanity-check the current dependency/runtime shape before answering: the tradeoff is mostly whether admin will stay inspection-first or quickly become an interactive workbench.
</details>

Yes. For the admin UI you described, starting with plain Go templates is likely a footgun.

It would be fine for a read-only “open files and show JSON” panel. But you asked for:

- classified logs with filtering/tailing
- store inspection across files/Qdrant/Honcho/model runs
- control-plane actions
- confirmations
- eventually more GUI surfaces

That becomes interactive state quickly. Without a frontend framework, we would either underbuild the UI or grow a pile of bespoke JS that is harder to replace later.

I’d revise the plan:

- Keep the admin backend in Go.
- Add a real frontend now: **Vite + Svelte + TypeScript + Tailwind**.
- Serve it from the Go admin server in dev/prod.
- Keep all admin data/control APIs in Go under `/admin/api/...`.
- Use the same API shape later for a player web UI, without coupling admin UI to game UI.

Why Svelte over React here: smaller surface, faster to build dense operator panels, less boilerplate, good enough for logs/tables/forms/state. React is also defensible, but Svelte fits this repo’s “small local tooling first” stage better.

So yes: no-framework is okay for a debug page, but for this admin workbench it would age badly.

Root cause: the Narrator commit contained human witness labels like `Admiral-Haruspex Veyr`. The bridge was treating every witness string as a Honcho peer ID, but Honcho only accepts `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`, so it returned 500.

- Added regression coverage in `bridge/tests/test_honcho_ops.py`.

Fixed. It was not the same root cause.

Old error: invalid Honcho peer IDs from human witness names.
New error: Honcho max observer limit. The commit path was adding every witness label as an observing peer, and this scene had 14 observers. Honcho allows 10.

Patch:
- `bridge/src/bridge/honcho_ops.py` now adds only actual event source peers, like `narrator` / player / surfaced actor peers, as session observers.
- Human witness labels still stay in metadata as `witness_labels`.
- `/v1/scene/commit` now returns a clean `503` detail instead of raw `500` if Honcho fails.
- Added regression test for crowded witness lists.

I also killed the currently running sidecar on `8787`, so the next `go run ./cmd/cli` will start a fresh bridge with this fix.

> turn the metabaron lore into a pluggable lore index.
> In the future we will add more ground lore, the game will present the ground lore as an option when starting a new story.

<details><summary>3 previous messages</summary>

> I’ll ground this in the current index/runtime shape first, then I’ll ask only for the product choices that aren’t discoverable from the repo. This should prevent us from planning a generic plugin system that fights the existing `sans_nom_lore` pipeline.
>
> A few facts from the repo: there is one hardcoded global source collection (`sans_nom_lore`), one hardcoded source artifact layout (`lore/canon/...`), and story state stores only `global_lore_collection`, not a lore-pack identity. The index builder is specifically Metabarons-shaped today, so “pluggable” is mainly about adding a lore-pack registry plus making the index builder/search/seed flow select a pack.
>
> Plan
>
> # Pluggable Ground Lore Index Plan
>
> ## Summary
> Turn the current Metabarons-only lore pipeline into a single-pack-per-story ground-lore system. Metabarons becomes the first `lore-pack`, and future packs can be added without changing story creation, retrieval, or UI wiring. New stories choose one ground-lore pack; the selected pack becomes the source-influence collection for seeding, context assembly, and runtime lore search.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a `LorePack` registry with tracked manifests under `lore/packs/<pack_id>/lore-pack.json`.
>   - Move current Metabarons artifacts under `lore/packs/metabarons/`.
>   - Pack manifest fields: `id`, `label`, `description`, `collection`, `embedding_model`, `artifact_roots`, `builder`, `smoke_queries`, `forbidden_literal_terms`, and `status`.
>   - Metabarons collection becomes `sans_nom_lore_metabarons`; keep `sans_nom_lore` as a temporary compatibility alias only where needed.
> - Refactor `lore-index` to operate by pack.
>   - Commands accept `--pack metabarons`; default is `metabarons`.
>   - `build`, `validate`, `ingest`, `smoke`, and `status` read pack manifests and write pack-local index artifacts under `lore/packs/<pack_id>/index/`.
>   - Keep the current Metabarons document builder, but move its source paths from hardcoded `lore/canon/...` to pack-manifest roots.
> - Update runtime story state and creation.
>   - Add `ground_lore_pack_id` and `ground_lore_collection` to `StoryState`.
>   - Keep reading old `global_lore_collection` for existing stories, but new stories use the ground-lore fields.
>   - Seed prompts and context rendering should name the selected pack as source influence, not assume Metabarons by name except when the selected pack is `metabarons`.
> - Add selection surfaces.
>   - TUI: `New Story` opens a lore-pack picker before story creation; each option shows label and description.
>   - CLI flags: add `-ground-lore-pack metabarons`; remove direct user-facing dependence on `-global-lore-collection` for normal story creation.
>   - Admin: expose `/admin/api/lore-packs`, show selected pack on story detail, and add a New Story control using the same app-layer `NewStory` action with pack selection.
> - Update retrieval.
>   - Runtime lore retrieval queries the selected pack collection plus the story collection.
>   - `-lore-search` accepts `-ground-lore-pack` and resolves the collection from the pack manifest.
>   - Admin external/status panel shows pack id, pack collection, story collection, and index status.
>
> ## Interfaces
> - New Go package or module area: `internal/lorepack`.
>   - `Pack`, `Registry`, `ListPacks(root)`, `GetPack(root, id)`, `DefaultPackID()`.
>   - `StoryActionOptions` gains `GroundLorePackID`.
>   - `StorySummary` includes `ground_lore_pack_id` for admin/resume display.
> - Bridge Python side:
>   - `lore-index --pack <id>` resolves manifest, source roots, output index dir, collection, and smoke queries.
>   - Metabarons-specific builder remains supported as `builder: metabarons_comics`.
>   - Future packs may start with a generic markdown/json builder, but that generic builder does not need to be fully implemented unless a fixture pack is added in tests.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Go:
>   - Pack registry loads `metabarons`, rejects duplicate/missing packs, and resolves collection names.
>   - Story creation persists selected `ground_lore_pack_id` and collection.
>   - TUI model selects a pack before returning `ActionNewStory`.
>   - Admin `/admin/api/lore-packs` returns available packs and story detail includes selected pack.
>   - Context assembly uses selected pack collection, not hardcoded `sans_nom_lore`.
> - Python:
>   - `lore-index --pack metabarons build/validate/status` works from moved paths.
>   - Stable doc ids and point ids remain unchanged except where source paths intentionally change.
>   - `ingest --pack metabarons --fake-embeddings` writes to `sans_nom_lore_metabarons`.
>   - Smoke queries are read from the pack manifest.
> - Integration:
>   - `go test ./...`
>   - `uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q`
>   - `npm run check && npm run build` in `admin`
>   - Manual: `go run ./cmd/cli` -> New Story -> choose Metabarons -> first turn uses that pack.
>   - Manual/admin: start `go run ./cmd/cli -admin`, create a story with Metabarons, verify story detail shows pack and collection.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - One story uses exactly one ground-lore pack.
> - Metabarons artifacts are physically moved under `lore/packs/metabarons/`.
> - Existing generated story dirs can remain readable through backward-compatible `global_lore_collection` handling.
> - The first implementation only needs one real pack: `metabarons`; the registry is built so future packs can be added without runtime code changes.
</details>

What changed:
- Writer refresh now hard-fails. No old-packet fallback after invalid Writer output.
- Writer runs now persist diagnostics under `data/stories/<story_id>/model-runs/writer/turn-000XXX/`:
  - `input.txt`
  - `raw-output.json`
  - `validation-error.txt` on failure
  - `accepted-packet.json` on success
  - `metadata.json`
- Player input is saved as pending state before Writer refresh.
- Writer failure marks the story as `blocked_writer_refresh` with artifact path and reason in `state.json`.
- Resume now backfills legacy stories to `metabarons` / `sans_nom_lore_metabarons` instead of preferring stale `sans_nom_lore`.
- Seed validation now rejects opening packets where first-choice branch nodes are all terminal without continuation notes.

- Clicking a log row shows full detail JSON, fields, and the full event.

Root cause: after the lore-pack split, runtime switched to `sans_nom_lore_metabarons`, but local Qdrant still only had the old `sans_nom_lore` collection.

I ingested the Metabarons pack:

```bash
uv run --project bridge lore-index --root . --pack metabarons ingest --replace
```

Result:
- `907` docs ingested into `sans_nom_lore_metabarons`
- Qdrant now lists `sans_nom_lore_metabarons`
- strict smoke passed, including:
  - `Bushitaka law`
  - `Lothar is Steelhead`
  - `Sans Nom ends the dynasty`

So `go run ./cmd/cli` should no longer hit that lore-search 503. If Qdrant storage gets wiped again, run `make lore-index-ingest`.

The seed retry now carries the previous raw Writer output into the next prompt and explicitly says: continue from this attempt, patch it, do not start a fresh story seed. That gives the Writer the actual broken packet with `node_cleansing_handoff` / similar missing targets in context instead of just a one-line error.

Implemented Mimo TTS for narrator turns.

Use it with:

```bash
go run ./cmd/cli -tts
```

It uses `XIAOMI__ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` by default, also supports `SANS_NOM_TTS_API_KEY`. Defaults match your example: `mimo-v2.5-tts`, voice `Milo`, WAV output.

Audio is saved per turn:

```text
data/stories/<story_id>/audio/turn-000001.wav
```

Added flags:

```text
-tts
-tts-endpoint
-tts-model
-tts-voice
-tts-instruction
-tts-output-dir
```

The turn record now stores `audio_path`, and logs include `tts.turn.request`, `tts.turn.completed`, and `tts.turn.failed` with request metadata and output path.

> # Plan: Stop Turn-1 Writer Refresh From Emitting Broken Future Targets
>
> ## Summary
> The turn-1 failure is a contract mismatch. The refresh Writer is allowed to produce a bounded `StoryPacket`, but its prompt and scenarist material do not clearly say that every `choice.target_node_id` must point to a node inside that same packet. The model creates “future” targets like `node_future_official_reprieve`; the validator correctly hard-fails. We will keep hard-fail behavior and prevent the bad packet shape with a clearer contract and better diagnostics.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Tighten the refresh Writer contract.
>   - Add the same packet-closure rule already used by seed generation to `WriterPrompt`: every `target_node_id` must resolve inside `nodes`.
>   - If a branch is an outbound handoff to a future packet, represent it as a terminal node with no choices and `revision_notes`, not as choices targeting missing future nodes.
>   - Keep the 3-5 node cap and hard validation; no repair loop and no auto-generated placeholder nodes.
>
> - Reinforce the contract in context assembly and scenarist workflow.
>   - Add a concise “StoryPacket closure rules” line to Writer context planning constraints.
>   - Update scenarist instructions so “choices” means pressure/options for the Writer to mine, not schema-valid `target_node_id`s.
>   - Add guidance to Writer’s tool usage: scenarist output is inspiration; Writer must convert it into a validator-closed packet.
>
> - Improve diagnostics for this exact failure mode.
>   - When Writer validation fails on a missing target, log the missing target, source node, choice id, and full known node id list in the event detail.
>   - Keep raw output and validation error artifacts as-is under `model-runs/writer/turn-*`.
>   - Add a clearer terminal error message pointing to the artifact dir and saying “missing target node inside bounded packet.”
>
> - Fix the turn record observability mismatch.
>   - Preserve `pending_decision` in `state.json` as today.
>   - Add the player’s post-turn choice/free text to the persisted turn record or log detail as `next_decision`, so the admin/log view shows that `choice_refuse_publicly` triggered the failed refresh.
>   - Do not change canon commit semantics; the rendered turn’s commit decision can remain the decision used to enter that node.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit tests:
>   - `WriterPrompt` includes packet-closure rules and terminal handoff guidance.
>   - `WriterContext.RenderText()` includes the same concise closure rule.
>   - Scenarist prompt clarifies that suggested choices are non-schema material.
>   - Missing-target validation diagnostics include node id, choice id, missing target, and known node ids.
>   - Persisted turn/log detail includes `next_decision` when a player choice triggers Writer refresh.
>
> - Regression tests:
>   - A fake refresh Writer packet with `node_future_*` targets hard-fails with no fallback and no auto-repair.
>   - A terminal handoff node with no choices and `revision_notes` passes validation.
>   - Seed prompt behavior remains aligned with refresh prompt behavior.
>
> - Verification:
>   - `go test ./...`
>   - `uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q`
>   - Manual rerun: start a story, choose a turn-1 option, confirm either a valid turn-2 packet is produced or the hard-fail diagnostic identifies the exact bad target cleanly.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - Hard fail remains the selected policy.
> - No Writer repair loop is added in this pass.
> - No post-processing mutates model output into valid shape.
> - Terminal handoff nodes with `revision_notes` are acceptable when the next packet should be generated from a fresh player decision.
</details>

The concrete failure is now pinned down:

- `WriterPrompt` for refresh does not include the “all `target_node_id`s must point to nodes in this same packet” rule. We only added that to the seed prompt.
- The Writer asked the scenarist for “3-5 scene nodes ... and choices”; the scenarist produced a useful free-form outline, but its last “Node 5” had outbound future choices.
- The Writer copied those future paths into real `Choice.target_node_id`s: `node_future_official_reprieve`, `node_future_unmeasured_below`, etc.
- `StoryPacket.Validate()` correctly rejects missing targets. This is not a model capability issue; it is a contract mismatch between prompt/scenarist material and the validator.
- The player decision is preserved in `state.json.pending_decision`; the persisted turn record showing empty `decision` is a separate observability flaw because it records the decision used to render turn 1, not the choice that triggered refresh.

>
> # MiniMax Async TTS For Full Narrator Turns
>
> ## Summary
> Replace the current synchronous MiMo chat-completions TTS path with MiniMax async long-form TTS, because the current response embeds base64 audio in a chat response and can truncate long narrator turns. The new path will submit the full narrator prose to MiniMax T2A Async, poll task status, download the generated audio file, and persist full diagnostics per turn.
>
> Docs basis: MiniMax Async Long TTS supports up to 1M input characters and async file retrieval; task creation uses `/v1/t2a_async_v2`, status uses `/v1/query/t2a_async_query_v2`, and audio download uses `/v1/files/retrieve_content`. Sources: [Async Long TTS Guide](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/guides/speech-t2a-async), [Create Task](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/speech-t2a-async-create), [Query Task](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/speech-t2a-async-query), [MiniMax CLI modality docs](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/token-plan/minimax-cli#usage-by-modality).
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a new async MiniMax TTS client under `internal/tts`.
>   - Use direct HTTP API, not shelling out to `mmx`, so game logs, artifacts, retries, and resume behavior stay deterministic.
>   - Auth uses `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, with env precedence: `SANS_NOM_TTS_API_KEY`, `MINIMAX_API_KEY`, `MINIMAX__ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `XIAOMI__ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`.
>   - Default base URL: `https://api.minimax.io`, override with `SANS_NOM_TTS_BASE_URL` / `-tts-base-url`.
>
> - Replace the turn synthesis flow.
>   - `-tts` submits `rollout.Draft.Prose` as raw async `text`.
>   - Default model: `speech-2.8-turbo`; configurable with `SANS_NOM_TTS_MODEL` / `-tts-model`.
>   - Default voice: `English_expressive_narrator`; configurable with `SANS_NOM_TTS_VOICE` / `-tts-voice`.
>   - Default output format remains `wav` for compatibility; add `-tts-format` with allowed `wav`, `mp3`, `flac`.
>   - Use audio settings: sample rate `32000`, bitrate `128000`, channel `2`, configurable later only if needed.
>
> - Persist complete TTS artifacts.
>   - Audio output: `data/stories/<story_id>/audio/turn-000001.<format>`.
>   - Diagnostics: `data/stories/<story_id>/model-runs/tts/turn-000001/`.
>   - Save `request.json`, `create-response.json`, `status.jsonl`, `download-response.json` when applicable, `error.txt` on failure, and `metadata.json` with task id, file id, usage characters, timing, output path, and text hash.
>   - Keep `TurnRecord.audio_path` pointing to the final audio file.
>
> - Poll and log visibly.
>   - Poll `processing` tasks every 2 seconds, respecting the documented 10 queries/sec limit.
>   - Default timeout: 15 minutes, configurable by `SANS_NOM_TTS_TIMEOUT_MS`.
>   - Emit classified log events: `tts.async.request`, `tts.async.status`, `tts.async.downloaded`, `tts.async.failed`.
>   - CLI prints progress lines such as `TTS task <id>: processing...` so it never appears stuck.
>
> - Keep CLI behavior simple.
>   - `go run ./cmd/cli -tts` still opens the TUI menu and enables TTS for selected/new stories.
>   - `-tts-instruction` is deprecated for async mode and kept only as legacy metadata; do not prepend instruction text into the spoken story.
>   - The old chat-completions client is removed from the live path. If kept at all, it is test-only or behind `-tts-mode chat` marked legacy.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit-test async client request shapes:
>   - create task sends Bearer auth, model, full text, voice settings, audio settings, and no chat message wrapper.
>   - query parses `processing`, `success`, `failed`, and `expired`.
>   - download writes raw audio bytes from `retrieve_content`.
>   - API/base_resp errors include response body snippets without secrets.
>
> - Unit-test CLI integration:
>   - `synthesizeTurnAudio` writes audio plus model-run artifacts.
>   - long text is not chunked or truncated before submit.
>   - failure preserves diagnostics and returns a clear error.
>   - `-tts` remains launcher-compatible.
>   - `TurnRecord.audio_path` uses the configured format extension.
>
> - Run verification:
>   - `go test ./...`
>   - `uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q`
>   - Manual live smoke: `go run ./cmd/cli -tts`, generate/read one long turn, confirm the saved audio contains the complete narrator text and logs show create/query/download details.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - Use MiniMax async direct API as the runtime implementation; `mmx speech synthesize` remains a useful manual reference, not the app backend.
> - Direct raw `text` input is enough for story turns; file upload is not implemented in v1 because the async API supports up to 1M characters directly.
> - Current `.env` token values are sufficient if accepted by MiniMax Bearer auth; if MiniMax rejects a token, the error will be surfaced with the endpoint and status but without leaking the token.
</details>

> # Multi-Turn Story Seed Workshop
>
> ## Summary
> Make story seeding closer to a real creative process: the seed Writer first produces several free-form workshop artifacts, then uses those artifacts plus source-lore influence to produce the final constrained `StoryBible + StoryPacket`. The free-form turns are saved under the story seed run folder as planning references, not canon.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a seed workshop phase before the final `SeedBundle` call.
>   - Save artifacts under `data/stories/<story_id>/model-runs/seed-workshop/` when a story id exists, or under the existing pre-story `seed-runs/<timestamp>/workshop/` path before workspace creation.
>   - Each turn writes `prompt.txt`, `output.md`, and `metadata.json`; final seed prompt receives a compact manifest of artifact paths plus short summaries, not the full raw text.
>   - Log `seed.workshop.request`, `seed.workshop.response`, and `seed.workshop.completed` with full prompt/output details.
>
> - Structure the Writer seed process into five turns:
>   1. **Imagination Turn**: free-form “what-if” exploration; generate 5-8 original story germs from lore influence without choosing one yet.
>   2. **Fiction Elements Turn**: select the strongest germ and develop character, POV, setting, plot pressure, theme, and style/tone as separate sections.
>   3. **Law And Suspension Turn**: design the original gravity law, social enforcement, taboo, cost, loopholes, visible consequences, and why the world believes it.
>   4. **Opening Scene Engine Turn**: design first-turn exposition, immediate pressure, player-world connection, sensory setting, choice pressures, and branch implications.
>   5. **Constrained Bundle Turn**: produce only the valid `SeedBundle` JSON using the existing schema and verifier loop.
>
> - Prompt rules for all free-form turns:
>   - Output Markdown, not JSON.
>   - No final `StoryPacket`, no schema fields, no `target_node_id`s.
>   - Treat Metabarons lore as craft DNA only: pressure, contradiction, body/law/taboo, witness-bound memory, operatic SF rhythm.
>   - Preserve originality: no canon names, factions, dynasty mechanics, council mode, direct equivalents, or all-cast fanout.
>   - Protect suspension of disbelief by making every strange element legible through social practice, cost, taboo, and consequence.
>
> - Keep final bundle validation strict.
>   - Final Writer prompt must cite the workshop manifest and explicitly say the workshop is advisory, not canon.
>   - Existing SeedVerifier continues to reject weak gravity law, missing player-world connection, literal canon import, malformed packet, and broken choice targets.
>   - If final JSON is invalid, retry with current context plus verifier feedback, not by regenerating the workshop from scratch.
>
> ## Prompt Turn Shapes
> - **Turn 1: Imagination**
>   - “Invent freely. Let ideas collide. Produce several original science-fantasy story germs, each with a vivid image, a taboo/law, a character wound, and a possible first crisis.”
> - **Turn 2: Elements**
>   - “Choose the strongest germ. Develop Character, POV, Setting, Plot, Theme, Style/Tone. Keep each element concrete and playable.”
> - **Turn 3: Law**
>   - “Stress-test the original gravity law. Explain enforcement, history, public rituals, edge cases, emotional cost, and why refusal matters.”
> - **Turn 4: Opening**
>   - “Design the opening turn as a scene engine: exposition, player identity, world connection, immediate pressure, sensory atmosphere, and 2-4 dramatic choices.”
> - **Turn 5: Bundle**
>   - “Using the workshop manifest, return only `{bible, packet}` JSON. Every choice target must resolve inside the bounded packet; future handoffs are terminal nodes with `revision_notes`.”
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit-test workshop orchestration:
>   - free-form turns write Markdown artifacts and metadata;
>   - final prompt receives artifact paths/manifest, not full raw workshop text;
>   - `-model-backend static` stays deterministic and does not call live providers.
> - Unit-test prompt content:
>   - each workshop turn includes its specific fiction craft goal;
>   - free-form turns forbid JSON/schema/target ids;
>   - final turn includes closure rules and advisory-only workshop language.
> - Regression-test seed retry behavior:
>   - verifier feedback revises the final constrained bundle without rerunning earlier workshop turns.
>   - workshop artifacts are not indexed as canon, not committed to Honcho, and not surfaced to Narrator.
> - Run:
>   - `go test ./...`
>   - `uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q`
>
> ## Assumptions
> - The Creative Writer owns all five turns; scenarist tools remain optional support inside those turns.
> - Workshop files are planning artifacts, not story canon.
> - The current Writer/Verifier loop remains; only the input process before final JSON becomes staged.
</details>

>   3. **Law And Suspension Turn**: design the original gravity law, social enforcement, taboo, cost, loopholes, visible consequences, and why the world believes it.
>   4. **Opening Scene Engine Turn**: design first-turn exposition, immediate pressure, player-world connection, sensory setting, choice pressures, and branch implications.
>   5. **Constrained Bundle Turn**: produce only the valid `SeedBundle` JSON using the existing schema and verifier loop.
>
> - Prompt rules for all free-form turns:
>   - Output Markdown, not JSON.
>   - No final `StoryPacket`, no schema fields, no `target_node_id`s.
>   - Treat Metabarons lore as craft DNA only: pressure, contradiction, body/law/taboo, witness-bound memory, operatic SF rhythm.
>   - Preserve originality: no canon names, factions, dynasty mechanics, council mode, direct equivalents, or all-cast fanout.
>   - Protect suspension of disbelief by making every strange element legible through social practice, cost, taboo, and consequence.
>
> - Keep final bundle validation strict.
>   - Final Writer prompt must cite the workshop manifest and explicitly say the workshop is advisory, not canon.
>   - Existing SeedVerifier continues to reject weak gravity law, missing player-world connection, literal canon import, malformed packet, and broken choice targets.
>   - If final JSON is invalid, retry with current context plus verifier feedback, not by regenerating the workshop from scratch.
>
> ## Prompt Turn Shapes
> - **Turn 1: Imagination**
>   - “Invent freely. Let ideas collide. Produce several original science-fantasy story germs, each with a vivid image, a taboo/law, a character wound, and a possible first crisis.”
> - **Turn 2: Elements**
>   - “Choose the strongest germ. Develop Character, POV, Setting, Plot, Theme, Style/Tone. Keep each element concrete and playable.”
> - **Turn 3: Law**
>   - “Stress-test the original gravity law. Explain enforcement, history, public rituals, edge cases, emotional cost, and why refusal matters.”
> - **Turn 4: Opening**
>   - “Design the opening turn as a scene engine: exposition, player identity, world connection, immediate pressure, sensory atmosphere, and 2-4 dramatic choices.”
> - **Turn 5: Bundle**
>   - “Using the workshop manifest, return only `{bible, packet}` JSON. Every choice target must resolve inside the bounded packet; future handoffs are terminal nodes with `revision_notes`.”
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit-test workshop orchestration:
>   - free-form turns write Markdown artifacts and metadata;
>   - final prompt receives artifact paths/manifest, not full raw workshop text;
>   - `-model-backend static` stays deterministic and does not call live providers.
> - Unit-test prompt content:
>   - each workshop turn includes its specific fiction craft goal;
>   - free-form turns forbid JSON/schema/target ids;
>   - final turn includes closure rules and advisory-only workshop language.
> - Regression-test seed retry behavior:
>   - verifier feedback revises the final constrained bundle without rerunning earlier workshop turns.
>   - workshop artifacts are not indexed as canon, not committed to Honcho, and not surfaced to Narrator.
> - Run:
>   - `go test ./...`
>   - `uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q`
>
> ## Assumptions
> - The Creative Writer owns all five turns; scenarist tools remain optional support inside those turns.
> - Workshop files are planning artifacts, not story canon.
> - The current Writer/Verifier loop remains; only the input process before final JSON becomes staged.

What changed:
- Removed the MiniMax async TTS client path.

- Default base URL is now `https://token-plan-sgp.xiaomimimo.com/v1`.

- TTS request shape is OpenAI-compatible chat completions:
  - `user` message = style/director instruction
  - `assistant` message = narrator prose to speak
  - `audio.voice` default = `Milo`
  - `audio.format` default = `wav`
- Long narrator turns are now chunked before synthesis to avoid MiMo output truncation:
  - default chunk size: `4500` chars
  - override: `SANS_NOM_TTS_CHUNK_CHARS`
  - each chunk writes its own `request.json`, `response.json`, and audio artifact
  - final turn writes one combined output file
  - for multi-chunk `wav`, chunks request `pcm16` internally and the app writes a valid WAV container

Docs used: [Xiaomi MiMo speech synthesis v2.5](https://platform.xiaomimimo.com/static/docs/usage-guide/speech-synthesis-v2.5.md)

Fixed the resume bug.

The play loop now saves a displayed turn to `pending-turn.json` before waiting for player input, marks the story state as `awaiting_player_choice`, and resumes from that checkpoint instead of rerolling/recommitting. When the player finally chooses, the pending turn is appended to `turns.jsonl` and cleared.

I also added recovery for old affected stories: if a story has narrator/commit logs but no pending turn, resume reconstructs the pending turn from the log detail. I exercised that against `data/stories/story-20260518-021057`; it now has a pending checkpoint and should resume at the already displayed Turn 1.

Yeah, I think the current injection is wrong for the workshop phase.

Main problems I see:

1. **Contradictory prompt layers**
   The top says: “free-form workshop, do not write StoryBible/StoryPacket.”
   Then the injected context says: “Return a durable StoryBible plus the first bounded StoryPacket.”
   That is training the model to half-workshop, half-final-output.

2. **Raw canon snippets are too literal**
   The context says “do not copy names,” but then feeds names like Tonto, Lothar, Othon, Castaka, Bushitaka, Metabaron, etc. Negative instruction is weaker than repeated source tokens. This makes literal drift more likely.

3. **The DNA is not distilled**
   The model gets lore summaries, but not the actual lesson:
   “law as social physics,” “body damage as lineage proof,” “ritual cruelty with philosophical justification,” “relationship pressure,” “refusal,” “witness-bound truth,” etc.

4. **Same context is reused for all workshop turns**
   Imagination, Elements, Law, and Opening need different context diets. The Imagination turn especially should not see packet closure rules or final schema language.

My suggestion:

- Keep **raw lore retrieval out of early workshop prompts**.
- Add a compact **Ground Lore DNA Brief** before the workshop:
  - 800-1500 words max.
  - Abstracted patterns only.
  - No canon proper nouns except maybe in hidden/source metadata, not prompt body.
  - Sections: `Law`, `Body/Technology`, `Family/Power`, `Refusal`, `Witness/Memory`, `Tone`, `What Not To Copy`.

Then per turn:

- **Imagination Turn**: only DNA brief + “invent 5-8 germs.” No schema, no raw snippets, no final-bundle rules.
- **Elements Turn**: DNA brief + previous germ output + fiction element checklist.
- **Law Turn**: DNA brief + selected germ + focused law/suspension-of-disbelief rubric.
- **Opening Turn**: selected seed material + opening-scene craft rules.
- **Final Bundle Turn**: workshop manifest + strict `SeedBundle` contract + packet closure rules.

If we still want retrieval, transform each hit into an **Influence Card** first:

```md
Source refs: wiki_lore:11, comic_volume:05
Pattern: A law becomes credible because everyone socially and physically reacts to it.
Craft lesson: The law must feel like infrastructure, not a game rule.
Avoid copying: no warrior caste, no Bushitaka name, no inherited mutilation ritual.
Useful pressure: a public refusal should endanger social reality, not just anger officials.
```

That is the right “DNA” shape. The Writer should receive patterns, not lore dumps.

> # Nerd Lore Expert Tool For Influence-Only Grounding
>
> ## Summary
> Add a cached `ask_lore_expert` tool that the Seed Writer and Refresh Writer can call when they need targeted Metabarons-derived craft analysis. The tool answers as a lore nerd and suspension-of-disbelief reviewer, not as a co-writer. It keeps raw lore out of the Writer’s default prompt and replaces broad source snippets with targeted, cached influence notes.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a lore expert tool layer.
>   - Tool name: `ask_lore_expert`.
>   - Available to seed workshop turns, final seed bundle turn, and Writer refresh.
>   - Not given to Narrator in this phase.
>   - Tool definition states clearly: answers are **influence material only**, not generated story canon, not StoryBible doctrine, not plot/prose to copy.
>
> - Tool request shape.
>   - Inputs: `pack_id`, `question`, `purpose`, optional `relevant_paths`, optional `avoid_terms`.
>   - `purpose` values: `law_mechanism`, `character_pressure`, `relationship_matrix`, `suspension_check`, `tone_pattern`, `anti_copy_check`, `general_influence`.
>   - Reject requests asking the expert to write final prose, final packet nodes, final StoryBible content, or direct equivalents of source canon.
>
> - Lore expert answer shape.
>   - Markdown artifact only, saved to disk.
>   - Fixed sections:
>     - `Influence-only answer`
>     - `Source pattern`
>     - `Why it works`
>     - `How to transform it originally`
>     - `Suspension-of-disbelief risks`
>     - `Do not copy`
>     - `Useful source refs`
>   - Every answer repeats that it is inspiration analysis, not canon for the generated story.
>
> - Replace broad workshop lore injection.
>   - Workshop prompts receive a compact lore-pack DNA brief and the `ask_lore_expert` tool instructions.
>   - Remove raw source-lore snippets from the default workshop prompt.
>   - Final constrained seed prompt receives workshop manifest plus lore expert artifact paths, not raw lore dumps.
>   - If no expert tool is used, the Writer still has enough high-level DNA to proceed.
>
> - Cold cache per lore pack.
>   - Cache path: `.cache/sans-nom/lore-expert/<pack_id>/<cache_key>/`.
>   - Cache files: `request.json`, `answer.md`, `sources.json`, `metadata.json`.
>   - `cache_key` includes pack id, pack manifest/index hash, question, purpose, relevant paths, prompt version, model/provider id.
>   - On cache hit, return without model call.
>   - Tool result returns `cached`, `answer_path`, `source_refs`, and a short preview; the Writer can read the file if needed.
>   - Add `.cache/` to `.gitignore`.
>
> - Logging and observability.
>   - Emit classified logs: `lore.expert.request`, `lore.expert.cache_hit`, `lore.expert.response`, `lore.expert.failed`.
>   - Log detail includes full request, cache key, selected source refs, prompt path, answer path, model metadata, and response preview.
>   - Admin log copy/detail view can inspect the complete request/answer path without bloating JSONL rows.
>
> ## Implementation Notes
> - Use the selected `ground_lore_pack_id`; do not hardcode Metabarons except as the current default pack.
> - The lore expert can use lore-index search plus pack artifact paths, but its output must be distilled craft analysis, not source summaries.
> - Default model can be the fast Codex OAuth path with high reasoning and priority tier; provider pooling can be added later if this becomes a bottleneck.
> - Existing `call_scenarists` remains for free creative outside pressure. `ask_lore_expert` is the opposite: grounded craft analysis and plausibility pressure.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Unit tests:
>   - tool rejects story-writing/final-packet requests;
>   - cache key changes when pack hash, prompt version, or question changes;
>   - cache hit avoids model call;
>   - tool result returns paths and preview, not full answer text;
>   - answer prompt requires influence-only framing and suspension-of-disbelief sections.
> - Regression tests:
>   - workshop prompt no longer includes raw broad source snippets by default;
>   - final seed prompt treats lore expert artifacts as advisory, not canon;
>   - cached expert answers are not indexed as story canon and are not committed to Honcho.
> - Smoke:
>   - run seed with a fake lore expert and verify artifact paths appear in final Writer context;
>   - run a live seed and verify logs show lore expert requests/cache hits with readable details.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - The tool is for Writer roles only in this phase.
> - Lore expert outputs are planning artifacts, not story canon.
> - The cache is local generated state and should not be committed.
> - The goal is less raw lore in context, more targeted source understanding when the Writer asks for it.
</details>

> # Fix Writer Gravity Bias
>
> ## Summary
> The Writer is not confused by “suspension of disbelief.” The main issue is our own seed contract: we repeatedly require an “original gravity law.” The model reads “gravity” literally, then reinforces itself through workshop summaries and lore-expert questions.
>
> Rename that concept to **binding doctrine**: a profound world rule with social, emotional, and material consequences, not necessarily physical gravity/weight/balance.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Replace prompt language:
>   - Change “original gravity law” to “original binding doctrine” in seed workshop, final seed, Writer refresh, verifier, and context text.
>   - Change “Law And Suspension Turn” to “Doctrine And Plausibility Turn.”
>   - Clarify “suspension of disbelief” means internal plausibility, social cause, emotional credibility, visible cost, and consequence.
>   - Add an explicit anti-default rule: do not use literal gravity, weight, counterweights, falling, anchors, scales, or balance unless the story truly needs that image.
>
> - Keep data structures stable:
>   - Do not migrate existing story files.
>   - Keep existing StoryBible law fields if they are structurally generic.
>   - Update validation errors/messages from “needs at least one original gravity law” to “needs at least one original binding doctrine.”
>
> - Tighten lore expert behavior:
>   - Lore expert answers should flag when a Writer question is over-literalizing “law” into gravity/weight mechanics.
>   - Lore expert should describe source-law patterns as consequence systems, initiation rules, taboos, oaths, inheritance pressures, refusal points, and social enforcement, not as gravity metaphors.
>
> - Prevent workshop propagation:
>   - Workshop artifact summaries should not preserve accidental gravity-heavy phrasing as if it were the chosen direction.
>   - Final seed prompt should say workshop material is advisory and the Writer may discard any motif that became too repetitive.
>

> # Behind-The-Scenes Office Chatroom
>
> ## Summary
> Add an admin “Behind The Scenes” view that turns model/log artifacts into a live office-chat transcript. Instead of raw rows, the system appears to mention roles like `@Writer`, `@Narrator`, `@Scenarist`, and `@LoreExpert`; responses appear as those roles. This is admin-only now, but the API shape marks messages for future gamer-safe exposure.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Add a transcript layer over existing logs.
>   - New backend mapper reads global logs, selected-story logs, detail JSON, and model-run artifacts, then emits `BackstageMessage` objects.
>   - Message fields: id, time, story_id, turn, run_id, role, speaker, kind, status, text, preview, source_event_id, detail_path, artifact_paths, and `visibility`.
>   - `visibility` defaults to `admin_only`; no gamer-facing route is added yet.
>
> - Add admin APIs.
>   - `GET /admin/api/backstage?tail=200` returns global backstage messages.
>   - `GET /admin/api/stories/{story_id}/backstage?tail=200` returns selected-story messages.
>   - `GET /admin/api/stories/{story_id}/backstage/stream?tail=50` streams SSE updates for the selected story; global gets the same `/admin/api/backstage/stream`.
>   - Stream can internally poll JSONL files every second; no new database.
>
> - Normalize existing events into chat.
>   - Seed workshop/writer/verifier request and response events become `@CreativeWriter`, `@NerdVerifier`, and system bubbles.
>   - Writer refresh started/completed/failed reads `model-runs/writer/.../input.txt`, `raw-output.json`, `validation-error.txt`, and metadata.
>   - Narrator rollout events become `@Narrator` response bubbles; narrator requests are logged before renderer calls so the chat shows active work.
>   - Scenarist tool events become system questions to `@Scenarist` and free-form Scenarist answer bubbles with material file links.
>   - Lore expert events become system questions to `@LoreExpert` and answer bubbles using cached answer paths.
>   - TTS events become `@Voice` request/progress/response bubbles.
>   - Errors render as failed bubbles with links to details.
>
> - Improve instrumentation where gaps exist.
>   - Add lightweight model-call request/response logs around Narrator, Actor, and Writer runner calls where only completion or artifact files exist today.
>   - Preserve existing JSONL/detail logs; do not duplicate large payloads into events when artifact paths already exist.
>   - Keep secret redaction through `gamelog`; transcript text is built from redacted detail/artifact data only.
>
> - Add Svelte UI.
>   - Add a `behind-scenes` tab before Logs.
>   - Render a dense chatroom: role badges, timestamp, run/turn chips, prompt/response cards, pending states, artifact links, and copy/open-detail actions.
>   - Auto-scroll when live mode is on; allow pause, tail size, role filter, and “show admin detail” toggle.
>   - Keep Logs tab unchanged for forensic raw inspection.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Go:
>   - Unit-test transcript mapping for seed writer, verifier, narrator, writer refresh, scenarist, lore expert, TTS, and failure events.
>   - Unit-test artifact loading uses safe story paths and rejects traversal.
>   - API tests for global backstage, story backstage, SSE headers/events, tail limit, and empty logs.
>   - Existing `go test ./...`.
>
> - Frontend:
>   - Add typed API helpers and compile-time checks for `BackstageMessage`.
>   - Build/typecheck admin: `npm run check && npm run build` in `admin`.
>   - Verify the view handles pending, completed, failed, and artifact-linked messages.
>
> - Manual smoke:
>   - Start `go run ./cmd/cli -admin`.
>   - Start a new story in another terminal.
>   - Confirm the Behind The Scenes tab shows live `@CreativeWriter`, `@LoreExpert`, `@Scenarist`, `@Narrator`, and error/status bubbles as calls happen.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - V1 is admin-only; future gamer exposure uses the same normalized message type but a filtered route later.
> - Existing JSONL logs remain the source of truth.
> - SSE is used for the chat feel, with polling as the internal file-watch mechanism.
> - No destructive controls are added in this pass.
</details>

3. **Better grouping**

4. **Tool-call visibility pass**
   - Make `@Writer -> @LoreExpert` and `@Writer -> @Scenarist` feel like natural chat, not just log-derived cards.

5. **Gamer-safe visibility model**
   - Keep `admin_only` now, but start tagging messages as future `gamer_safe`, `spoiler`, `internal_prompt`, `tool_material`, etc.

6. **Replay fixture tests**
   - Save a few real log folders as test fixtures.

> why is the `@LoreExpert` marked as called by system ? its not a Writer call?
>
> User context
>
> Images:
> - `/var/folders/93/ffgnm9417y1f4f23q9rhr9p80000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_cTUzoS/Screenshot 2026-05-18 at 14.49.48.png`

Yes, that should be a Writer call.

Right now it is marked `@System` because the backstage mapper is too dumb: `lore.expert.request` is logged by the tool implementation, not by the Writer event itself, and the event does not carry a `caller_role` / `parent_run_id`. So the UI falls back to “System asked @LoreExpert”.

What actually happened in that screenshot is most likely:

`@CreativeWriter` prompt runs
`CreativeWriter` calls `ask_lore_expert` tool
runtime logs `lore.expert.request`
backstage mapper renders it as `@System -> @LoreExpert`

So: runtime behavior is probably correct, transcript attribution is wrong.

The fix should be:
- add `caller_role: creative-writer | writer | seed-workshop | ...`
- add `parent_event_id` or `parent_run_id`
- render tool requests as:
  - `@CreativeWriter -> @LoreExpert ...`

> we have a problem with how the scenarist are used there.
>
> the requests will not work when done in parrallel because each requests either require the previous request answer to be answerable, or they would be more sensible if they knew the previous answer.
>
> ------------
>
> two way we can approach the issue:
>
> - make the call synchronous and provide the previous answer(s) to the next context
> - update the agent tool instructions to explain each request should be independent or made separately if they depends on each others..
>
> what you think ?

I’d take the second path as the default.

`call_scenarists` is explicitly a parallel workshop tool. Requests inside one call should be independent lenses on the same problem. If request B needs request A’s answer, the Writer should make call A, read the files, then make call B with those files as `relevant_paths`.

I would not make a single tool call secretly synchronous. That hides execution semantics, makes provider-pool behavior less obvious, and turns one “parallel brainstorm” call into an implicit mini-agent loop. The Writer already has the right control loop: call scenarists, inspect outputs, decide what follow-up to ask.

What I’d change:

1. Tool description:
   “Requests in one call run in parallel and do not see each other’s answers. Put only independent requests in the same call. For dependent work, call this tool again after reading the returned files.”

2. Scenarist schema field descriptions:
   Make `requests` say “parallel independent requests.”

3. Writer prompt:
   “After `call_scenarists`, read returned files before making dependent follow-up requests or choosing a direction.”

4. Tool response note:
   “These materials were generated independently. For synthesis or follow-up, read the files and call again with those paths.”

5. Optional warning, not rejection:
   If multiple requests in the same call include phrases like “selected germ”, “strongest germ”, “prior”, “previous”, “best candidate”, log `scenarist.call.dependency_warning`. Useful for observability, but don’t block the Writer.

So: parallel stays parallel. Sequential reasoning stays with the Writer. This keeps the workshop tool honest and makes the Writer do the editorial synthesis, which is exactly the job boundary we want.

> how do i run the install in bridge on my env?

From repo root:

```bash
uv sync --project bridge
```

That installs the bridge dependencies into `bridge/.venv` using `bridge/pyproject.toml` and `bridge/uv.lock`.

Then verify:

```bash
uv run --project bridge python -c "import honcho, qdrant_client, voyageai; print('ok')"
uv run --project bridge pytest bridge/tests -q
```

If your editor still complains after that, restart basedpyright/Python language server so it picks up `pyrightconfig.json`.

> Plan
>
> # Plan: Make Seed Quality Dramatic, Not Just Valid
>
> ## Summary
>
> Keep the multi-turn seed workshop, but change its job from “build a plausible doctrine” to “discover a playable dramatic engine.” The final Writer should use workshop artifacts only, produce one valid bundle, and pass through a taste/verifier gate that rejects boring procedural worldbuilding even when schema is valid.
>
> ## Key Changes
>
> - **Separate creative exploration from final packaging**
>   - Workshop turns and scenarists keep tools enabled.
>   - Final `SeedBundle` Writer gets read-only workshop/scenarist files and `ask_lore_expert`, but no `call_scenarists` by default.
>   - If final bundle validation fails, retry only for structural repair. If the bundle is valid but weak, a verifier/taste gate rejects with targeted creative feedback.
>
> - **Change workshop shape**
>   - Turn 1 keeps several story germs.
>   - Turn 2 should not immediately choose one “strongest” germ. It should compare 2-3 finalists across player desire, first irreversible act, antagonist pressure, emotional clarity, and novelty.
>   - Turn 3 becomes “dramatic engine and player hook,” not mainly doctrine stress.
>   - Turn 4 designs the opening around one sharp player dilemma: what the player can do now that cannot be undone.
>
> - **Add a Dramaturg/Playtester verifier**
>   - Reject seeds where the opening is mostly procedure, exposition, invented civic vocabulary, or system explanation.
>   - Require the first turn to include: visible player desire, an immediate irreversible pressure, at least one active opposing will, and choices that express stance rather than only route.
>   - Require each choice to cost something personal, social, or material immediately.
>
> - **Let characters drive the first scene**
>   - Seed can still avoid full actor peer cards, but it should create mini actor briefs for the first-turn cast: desire, leverage, fear, what they will do if ignored.
>   - Narrator context should receive these as surface behavior guidance.
>   - First turn should include at least one character making a move against or around the player, not only presenting tokens/warrants/offers.
>
> - **Reduce jargon density**
>   - Add a seed verifier check for invented-term load in the first narrator turn and packet beats.
>   - Prefer concrete noun/action pairs over abstract civic-system terms.
>   - Keep the binding doctrine, but require it to be demonstrated through conflict before being explained.
>
> ## Test Plan
>
> - Unit tests:
>   - final seed Writer runner excludes `call_scenarists`;
>   - workshop turns still allow scenarist and lore expert tools;
>   - verifier rejects valid-but-flat seeds with no active opposing will;
>   - verifier rejects first turns where choices are only route/inspection choices;
>   - verifier accepts a structurally valid opening with a clear player desire, antagonist pressure, and irreversible choice.
>
> - Regression tests:
>   - schema validation and missing-target hard-fail behavior stay unchanged;
>   - seed retry still patches the current failed bundle instead of restarting;
>   - narrator still receives a valid bounded packet and does not see workshop material.
>
> - Manual smoke:
>   - run `go run ./cmd/cli`;
>   - confirm seed time drops because final Writer does not call scenarists;
>   - inspect backstage: workshop has creative calls, final bundle is direct;
>   - first narrator turn should read less like civic documentation and more like a playable scene with a human conflict.
>
> ## Assumptions
>
> - We keep hard validation and no automatic repair loop for Writer refresh.

I checked `story-20260518-104142` and the seed run behind it. My read: the Narrator is not the main failure. It faithfully rendered a seed that had already collapsed into “procedural civic weirdness.”

Main causes:

- The workshop converged too early. Turn 1 generated several germs, then every later turn and scenarist call kept asking for “strongest germ / doctrine / plausibility,” so the same idea got reinforced instead of challenged.
- The final constrained Writer still had `call_scenarists`, so after a 4-turn workshop it launched more scenarists. That made the seed slow and kept stirring the same soup.
- The retry loop fixed schema, not taste. Iteration 1 had invalid missing targets; iteration 2 was told to preserve the same story and patch it. That is correct for structure, but it locks in a mediocre premise.
- The verifier accepted validity, not entertainment. It returned `accepted:true` with no visible critique. It did not reject “too procedural,” weak player desire, passive choices, or overloaded invented nouns.
- The packet choices are errands, not dramatic commitments: go nursery / go neighbor / go patron / give Sova tool. They branch location and priority, but not a sharp player stance.
- Actor agents are absent in seed, so named characters behave as pressure labels. Hess, Sova, Mara, Surren exist, but nobody has enough agency to make the scene spark.
- The “binding doctrine” machinery is still dominating the creative frame. It produces plausible systems, but plausibility alone is giving us careful civic bureaucracy instead of story heat.
