>     "player_world_connection": "Iri-Ka is an original internal figure allowed by the scenario contract: a Metabunker servant-custodian whose keys open initiation apparatus, artificial-milk organs, and witness rails. They cannot overrule Aghora, but because Bushitaka needs witnesses, their choices can contaminate or preserve legitimacy.",
>     "world_basics": [
>       "The Metabunker is the dynasty's mobile fortress and household: a warship, archive, nursery, surgical theater, and temple of weapons at once.",
>       "The Bushitaka demands visible, irreversible bodily proof; private courage does not count unless witnesses can remember the cost.",
>       "The Metabaronic succession should pass through lethal combat against the predecessor, but Aghora's succession over Storlon-bodied Steelhead is secretly compromised.",
>       "No-Name is the young heir, born of Aghora's impossible father-mother body and destined for the final Metabaronic line, but in this opening he does not yet understand the old breach.",
>       "Aghora is both loving parent and reigning Metabaron; their mercy toward Steelhead became a hidden fault that now pressures No-Name's initiation.",
>       "Tonto is a robot witness and household narrator whose recordings can outlive masters, servants, and official lies.",
>       "Original servants, custodians, and witness-keepers may exist inside the household when they support rather than replace canon dynamics.",
>       "External powers such as the Empire, Techno-Technos, Ekonomats, and Shabda-Oud would exploit any sign that Metabaron legitimacy is wounded."
>     ],
>     "lore_principles": [
>       {
>         "id": "lp_visible_cost",
>         "name": "Legitimacy Requires Visible Cost",
>         "description": "A claim to power is not persuasive until the household sees an irreversible mark on a body and remembers who caused it.",
>         "source_pattern": "Othon's cybernetic pelvis, Aghnar's crushed feet, Aghora's altered body and bionic hand, and No-Name's ear initiation all make legitimacy bodily and witnessed.",
>         "enforcement": "Rites, weapon locks, witness recordings, and family speech all treat unmarked intention as worthless. A cost must be visible enough for servants and enemies to repeat.",
>         "why_profound": "The dynasty cannot separate soul, law, and flesh; every moral claim becomes anatomy.",
>         "not_merely_cruel": "The wound is a social proof mechanism: it creates an archive, a witness, and a debt, not just pain for pain's sake."
>       },
>       {
>         "id": "lp_witness_memory",
>         "name": "Witnesses Manufacture Memory",
>         "description": "A witness in this world is never neutral furniture. The one who records the wound can preserve or contaminate succession.",
>         "source_pattern": "Tonto's frame narration, the Crest of Castaka's inherited memory, and repeated witnessed initiation scenes make memory an active force.",
>         "enforcement": "Tonto, servants, servo-witnesses, and household custodians decide what can later be told as true; killing or silencing a witness is itself a public confession of fear.",
>         "why_profound": "Power depends on the weak remembering the strong accurately enough to make them legitimate.",
>         "not_merely_cruel": "Servants matter because without them the dynasty has no archive, no ceremony, and no proof that sacrifice happened."
>       },
>       {
>         "id": "lp_failed_escape",
>         "name": "Mercy Becomes the Next Wound",
>         "description": "Every attempted escape from Bushitaka pushes the wound forward into the next generation.",
>         "source_pattern": "Aghnar tried to keep his son from the tradition; Honorata overrode him. Aghora could not kill Steelhead and hid the failure from No-Name.",
>         "enforcement": "Mercy, concealment, or refusal never vanish; they return as harsher training, illegitimate succession pressure, or demands for compensatory sacrifice.",
>         "why_profound": "The family machine punishes not only cruelty but also incomplete mercy.",
>         "not_merely_cruel": "The tragedy is not that the code simply loves violence, but that even love is translated into a future body's debt."
>       },
>       {
>         "id": "lp_body_weapon_family",
>         "name": "Body, Weapon, Family Are Inseparable",
>         "description": "Weapons, bodies, and family names are one system. A weapon can be an heir, a servant can be an archive, and a body can be a legal document.",
>         "source_pattern": "Oko mini-bombs, Praxis, Superkolt, metacraft linkage, cybernetic implants, and the Metabunker's domestic machinery all fuse identity with weaponry.",
>         "enforcement": "Initiation apparatus only responds to keyed flesh, old scars, blood, prosthetics, and recorded witness cadence; abstract argument cannot open the rite.",
>         "why_profound": "The dynasty's intimacy is mechanical; love and maintenance happen through devices built to injure.",
>         "not_merely_cruel": "The strange technology feels lived-in because everyone uses it as household infrastructure: lamps, locks, milk organs, slicers, records, prosthetics."
>       },
>       {
>         "id": "lp_law_cannot_parse_anomaly",
>         "name": "The Law Breaks on What It Cannot Name",
>         "description": "Aghora's succession breach is dangerous because the Bushitaka has no clean grammar for an indestructible predecessor and a father-mother heir.",
>         "source_pattern": "Aghora could not kill Storlon-bodied Steelhead, sealed and ejected him instead, and later raised No-Name without revealing that failure.",
>         "enforcement": "The household compensates with secrecy, stronger rites, and pressure on No-Name's body rather than admitting the law failed.",
>         "why_profound": "The most important truth in the room is not merely hidden; it is structurally unspeakable in the dynasty's language.",
>         "not_merely_cruel": "Aghora's concealment is not random villainy; it is an impossible parent trying to keep a child inside a code that cannot describe them."
>       }

Yes, your read is right. The Writer was not starting from scratch logically, but the prompt was telling it to behave like a fresh seed pass anyway.

What happened:

- The retry prompt included the previous output and verifier feedback.
- But the same generic seed rules still said: “Before drafting any StoryBible or StoryPacket, do a lore orientation pass,” then listed the full navigation flow.
- So the Writer followed both instructions: it kept the previous output in context, then re-ran the lorepack read sequence before patching. Annoyingly obedient little loop.

I fixed that by splitting the seed prompt into two modes:

- First attempt: full lore orientation required.
- Repair attempt: no full re-orientation; start from previous raw output, patch only what validation requires, and use targeted lore reads or LoreExpert only for specific unresolved feedback.

Fixed and pushed `da10935` to `main`.

What happened: the runtime Writer refresh hit the 24 local-tool safety cap because it started doing a seed-style research pass again: listing staged files, reading `story/context.txt`, rereading multiple narration files, reading `lorepack/navigation.md`, then browsing lore volumes. It never got back to producing the next packet.

I changed two things:

- Runtime Writer prompt now treats assembled context as authoritative and forbids default lorepack re-orientation during refresh. Lorepack reads are still allowed, but only as targeted checks.
- A story blocked by `blocked_writer_refresh` now retries the Writer refresh once on the next run when refresh is enabled, instead of immediately hard-stopping on the old blocked state.

Verified:

- `go test ./...`
- `git diff --check`

Your current story should now be able to recover by rerunning:

```bash
go run ./cmd/cli --tts
```

It should retry the blocked turn-7 Writer refresh with the tighter prompt. If it fails again, it will stay blocked with the new artifact path rather than looping.

>
> ## Architecture — Solid Core, 3 Real Problems
>
> **Good:**
> - Go/Python split is principled and enforced. Python sidecar stays bounded to 6 endpoints.
> - `StoryPacket` validator is the strongest piece of code in the repo — structural rules, not just null checks. `ValidateCanonOnly()` enforcing the planning/canon boundary is rare discipline.
> - Writer → Narrator split is correct for this IP. Structure separate from voice.
> - `agentfs` scoping works for Writer. Atomic writes. Clean Go throughout.
>
> **Problem 1 — motif detection is broken:**
> `detectSpentMotifs()` in `progression.go` does keyword matching. Keywords like "witness", "scar", "blood", "hand" — the permanent vocabulary of Metabarons — fire as "spent" after turn 1. Writer then avoids that vocabulary. The heuristic measures token density, not narrative phase. This silently degrades every story.
>
> Fix: make Writer set `current_arc_phase` + `spent_motifs` in packet metadata. Progression reads Writer-owned metadata, not prose text.
>
> **Problem 2 — no schema sync pipeline:**
> Go structs ↔ Pydantic models in `bridge/models.py` are manually synced. ADR 0001 promised a generation path. It's not there. Maintenance time-bomb.
>
> **Problem 3 — Scenarist reads absolute paths:**
> Writer correctly uses scoped relative paths. Scenarist leaks absolute `/Users/vincent/dev/sans-nom/data/stories/...` paths. Breaks agentfs policy for that role.
>
> ---
>
> ## Game Design — 2 Things Work, 3 Don't
>
> **Works:**
> - The 5 lore principles (`visible_cost_proof`, `witness_memory_law`, etc.) do real design work. Choice structure from turn 2 onward is genuinely differentiated.
> - Choice labeling is strong: player sees consequences in the verb, not menu labels. "Burn the germ-cord in your bare hand" carries what the choice costs before the player commits.
>
> **Problem 1 — cosmetic choices are dead weight:**
> Turn 1 has 3 choices, all target same node, Narrator receives no signal about which was picked. Player gets illusion of agency at entry. Fix is one line: surface `decision.ChoiceID` into the Narrator's context prompt.
>
> **Problem 2 — no prose bridge between Writer refresh boundary:**
> Turn 3 ends mid-scene. Turn 4 starts same moment from different angle. Loading spinner exposes the seam. A static prose bridge from the terminal node's `revision_notes` would make the gap feel intentional.
>
> **Problem 3 — `ForbiddenCanonTerms()` does nothing:**
> Defined in `story/types.go`, returned by a function, never called in any validation path. It's decorative. Either enforce it post-seed or remove it.
>
> ---
>
> ## Story Quality — Turn 1–6
>
> Genuinely good. Specific:
>
> **Turn 3 is the strongest.** "You do not give it a wound. You give it a verdict." That's the Bushitaka logic made flesh in one sentence. The data-tooth survival is well-planted. The ant-robot image is strange and precise.
>
> **Turn 6 logic is sound.** "The proof has become a tool; the tool has become a gate; the gate is open only because part of you was ruined in public." — this is the accumulated consequence design working correctly. Player's choices (burn → public decode → pending) have a coherent moral profile.
>
> **Player character works.** Veyra Qal is original, correctly positioned in the household hierarchy, not contradicting canon. Her emerging logic — public accountability over private custody — is readable and consistent across 6 turns.
>
> **Lore fidelity: high.** No canon characters named directly (correct for `canon_internal_original` mode). Crest logic, Bushitaka succession rules, witness-engines as active legitimacy enforcers — all rendered correctly. The story feels like Jodorowsky without being a retelling.
>
> **One real prose problem:** Turn 3 is a wall of text — no paragraph breaks. The Narrator prompt has no paragraph structure rule. Excellent content, unreadable formatting. Add explicit 2–4 paragraph break requirement to Narrator prompt.
>
> **Minor:** Turns 5 prose over-explains the Crest-null result in 3 formulations that say the same thing. Jodorowsky names once and lets weight rest.
>
> ---
>
> ## Biggest Near-Term Risk
>
> `detectSpentMotifs()` will corrupt Writer context silently in every story, causing it to shy away from the exact vocabulary Metabarons requires. Fix this before adding more stories.
>
> **Second risk:** Honcho representations are empty strings for all turns so far. Narrator runs on packet context only. Fine at turn 6. Will hollow out character differentiation by turn 15+ if actor cards never seed.
>
> ---
>
> ## Priority Order
>
> 1. Fix motif detection (Writer-owned metadata, not keyword scan)
> 2. Surface cosmetic choice ID to Narrator
> 3. Enforce `ForbiddenCanonTerms()` or delete it
> 4. Add paragraph structure rule to Narrator prompt
> 5. Fix Scenarist absolute path leak
> 6. Prose bridge between Writer refresh boundary

Fixed. The resumed-story Writer refresh was failing because I made `packet.metadata` an open string map, and the strict response-format schema path rejects that shape before the model runs.

I changed it to a closed object with fixed required string fields:

- `current_arc_phase`
- `next_arc_phase`
- `spent_motifs`

I also added a recursive strict-schema test so any response schema with “required/property mismatch” or open object maps fails locally before it reaches the Codex backend.

- `go test ./internal/prompt ./internal/writer ./cmd/cli`
- `go test ./...`
- `git diff --check`

> ## New Turns 7–10 — Quality
>
> **Turn 7 is the best individual piece of writing in the whole story.** "Black fissures crawl from the bite in crooked ant-tracks" is precise and physical. The QA-9 revelation is well-constructed: firmware swapped in the maintenance rookery, not under surgical oversight — inside hands, not outside hands, doing the cut. And then this:
>
> > *fear of the house, and of what it is teaching you to become: a witness who preserves truth by consuming whatever still lives close enough to speak.*
>
> That's the moral logic of Veyra Qal's entire arc named at exactly the right moment. Best line across all 10 turns.
>
> **Turn 8 — solid connective tissue.** The rookery as space is well-built (calibration teeth worn smooth, molted ant-shells sorted by family). The filing engine calling QA-9 "a consumed witness" rather than broken tool is exact Metabarons bureaucratic logic. Choice design holds — three trails, all passing through the wound.
>
> **Turn 9 — too short.** The band-split mechanic is strong ("leaves half under Iri's skin, rivets the other half through you"). "When she steps down from the rail, she does not step free" is good. But the turn resolves the split quickly and exits. Compared to turns 3 and 7, it reads like a connector, not a scene. Not broken, just thin.
>
> **Turn 10 — strong close.** "You have made your skin into a corridor for the house to walk through" — excellent. The exterior pulse now beating in time with the split band is the right escalation. The timing: someone outside began asking during the exact surgical minutes. That's the conspiracy closing.

Confirmed against the live resumed story artifacts.

The new Writer packets do set progression metadata now. `turn-000008` and `turn-000009` both have `packet.metadata.current_arc_phase`, `next_arc_phase`, and `spent_motifs`. The older refresh packets from `turn-000003` and `turn-000005` are empty because they were generated before the schema fix.

The remaining issue was real: the Writer context still converted every bible open thread into `Keep open thread active`, even after packet metadata showed several mechanisms were already spent. I changed [progression.go](./internal/contextbundle/progression.go) so once a refreshed packet has enough authored spent motifs and multiple open threads, guidance switches to:

- close/disprove/merge/make costly at least one existing open thread
- don’t introduce a new investigation shadow unless it resolves/transforms an existing one

I verified this directly with the current resumed story via context preview: `story-20260522-081234` now shows `Narrowing phase...` and lists the open threads as closure candidates.

I also added the Narrator branch-continuation rule in [templates.go](./internal/prompt/templates.go): branch continuations need real scene weight, not transition-summary compression. That targets the turn 9 thinness.

- `ForbiddenCanonTerms()` is gone, not enforced as a stale/decorative hardcoded list.

> ---
>
> ## What the Commits Show
>
> `fix(writer): use authored progression metadata` — motif detection fix landed. `fix(writer): narrow open threads after spent motifs` — the Writer now gets a signal to converge. `feat: add master lore summary support in lorepacks` — LORE.md I wrote is wired in. Those three matter most.
>
> ---
>
> ## Turns 11–16 — Quality
>
> **Turn 11: strong.** Wake-path environment is precise — "racks of replacement mandibles hang like rows of devotional teeth." The listening fork discovery is the story's cleanest plot mechanism so far: Iri's voice arriving half a breath too soon. **Best line: "The house did not need her betrayal, only her routine."** That's the whole conspiracy in one sentence.
>
> **Turn 12: remarkable, but structurally wasted.** Contains the most direct moral confrontation in 16 turns: *"no choice made in the name of saving her will be clean unless you can say what kind of saving still leaves a person hers."* But it's a terminal node — choice: none. The story asks Veyra the hardest question then doesn't let the player answer it. This should be a reflection node or carry a `[Reflect]` verb. Right now the accusation dissolves into atmosphere.
>
> **Turn 13: tight.** The listening fork "dangling from your vitrified hand like a snapped insect mandible" lands. Better: the exterior relay synchronizing to the sluice rhythm. "Whoever wants the preserved remnant is no longer merely listening. They are counting the breaths before the rookery opens." — the threat has graduated from surveillance to acquisition. Right escalation.
>
> **Turn 14: best of the new batch.** Opening move — Veyra demands public consent before the Sept takes Iri's wrist — is the fix from last review working: decision-making process now foregrounded rather than implied. **"Consent is recorded. It does not soften the metal."** Best single line in the new turns. The conspiracy timeline clicks into place cleanly: command harvested during service, not during surgery; QA-9 carried it in, scrubbed 67 seconds after Crest-null tag. And then this: *"biological continuity, no Crest confirmation required, purchaser accepts theological dispute."* That's the most sophisticated worldbuilding in the story. Someone is building a market for fake succession — selling narrative continuity to buyers who don't care about the Crest. Very Jodorowsky.
>
> **Turn 15: functional.** Countdown mechanism works. Three choices well-differentiated. "Enemies will hear the truth before the lie—but so will every power hungry enough to turn a living remnant into a war of succession" is honest about the broadcast choice's cost. Slightly thinner than turns 13–14 but not a problem.
>
> **Turn 16: delivers the key reveal.** "The sale-language calling it continuation was added afterward." — the germ-cord was never a real succession threat. The Crest-null tag predates the preservation claim. Someone manufactured the evidence of lineage, not the lineage itself. This is the Bushitaka's specific enemy: fraud dressed as cost. Lore-precise. The "nine minutes" countdown gives it urgency.
>
> ---
>
> ## One New Problem
>
> The nine-minute countdown is the wrong register. Every prior piece of urgency in this story arrives as architecture — "the verdict does not fall like a blade, it closes like architecture" (turn 5). The Metabunker doesn't tick. The Gnomon Sept doesn't set timers; it accumulates weight. A nine-minute clock is thriller pacing inside an opera. It'll work mechanically but it undercuts the specific quality this story has earned. Better: the packet clears when the relay repeats a threshold number of times, or when the next witness-cycle closes, or when something biological changes — not minutes on a clock.
>
> ---
>
> ## What the Convergence Fix Did
>
> It worked. Turns 11–16 closed down from three open threads (QA-9, relay, Iri's band) to one coherent conspiracy: voice-harvest → command-theft → manufactured claim → external buyer. The Writer narrowed. The arc is visible now. That's the metadata fix doing its job.
>
> ---
>

"Being spared is not the same as being believed" is her best line and it's also her only fully-formed sentence across 16 turns. She's ready for an actor card.
